build: Apex disk release, the contributor's own G64 images of both sides; sha256 of each in orientation.md

exclude: zero page: the processor port and the game's variables, all written at run time; at the hand-over it holds what the loader left
6 parts: Cherryland, Jellyland, Pipeland and others
elsewhere: 6 parts: Cherryland, Jellyland, Pipeland and others

comments.text: The 6510's data-direction register. Nothing in the game reads it as code: the JSR at $1C32 and the JMP at $CBC6 are assembled with $0000 and have their real targets written in before they run.

Object slots, table 1 of 5 at $0200-$024A (15 slots each, indexed by slot X; the other per-slot tables are at $F4xx-$F9xx). Read position in the slot's movement script: $C282 reads the script byte at ($47),Y with Y from here and increments it; $FE in the script holds it, $FD runs $C55A. Cleared when a slot is spawned ($EBD5).

Object slots, table 2 of 5 (15 slots): a second script read position, stepped the same way as $0200 by the code at $C43B-$C4E2; cleared at spawn ($EBD8), by $C5E5 when $C5D2 points the slot at a new script (with $022D), and by $C830 (with $0200).

Object slots, table 3 of 5 (15 slots): written by $C482, $C67F, $C931, $CAF9, read as an index by $C900, and incremented by $C597-$C59C (LDA/STA $021E,Y); cleared at spawn ($EBC6). Meaning not traced from this range.

Object slots, table 4 of 5 (15 slots): index into the slot's animation list at ($80),Y: $B697 steps it and wraps to 0 when the next entry is $10 or more; cleared at spawn ($EBCF) and by $C5E8 when the slot gets a new script; $BAB5 sets it to $FF when $BAA1 gives the slot a new animation list, so the next step starts at entry 0.
Object slots, table 5 of 5 (15 slots): nonzero while the slot is in use. Spawning writes 1 ($EC05); $B647, $BA23, $C198 and the object code at $C36E-$C8AC skip a slot holding 0.

$024B-$02A6: the KERNAL's own work area (file tables, keyboard buffer at $0277, memory bounds at $0281-$0284, colour and key-repeat bytes, the PAL flag at $02A6), left as the KERNAL set it before the game switched the ROM out ($196C). No instruction in the engine reads or writes it.
16 bytes, alternately $FD and $FE: glyph numbers copied by $3C62 (the screen set-up loop $3C28-$3C84) to screen $46DC-$46EB.
16 glyph numbers $DE-$ED in order, copied by $3C6E to screen $459C-$45AB.
The same 16 glyph numbers $DE-$ED rotated by eight ($E6-$ED, $DE-$E5), copied by $3C74 to screen $45EC-$45FB.
$02D7-$02FF, zero; no reader or writer found in the engine.
$0300-$0313: BASIC's vectors and work bytes as left at boot. The game never calls BASIC (the ROM is switched out in play); no reader found.
KERNAL IRQ vector, low byte. $1809 ($182D) writes $68 or $62 here (with $18 in $0315) so a ROM-in interrupt reaches the game's dispatcher $1868 or $1862.
KERNAL IRQ vector, high byte, written by $1833.
$0316-$0317 BRK vector and $031A-$0333 the KERNAL's file and I/O vectors, as left at boot; the game does not use them with the ROM out.

KERNAL NMI vector, low byte: $197F stores $C1 here at start-up (the high byte $FE is left), pointing the RESTORE key's NMI at $FEC1 in the KERNAL ROM (the end of its NMI routine in the standard ROM: an RTI), so RESTORE is ignored while the ROM is in; with the ROM out the NMI goes through $FFFA instead.
Music driver on/off: 0 stops the tune; $080C clears it, $0584 increments it once the tune is set up, $0591 clears it when a tune ends. $087B plays a frame only while it is nonzero.

The music driver's per-frame work (called through $0880). Advances the tempo counter $08A0 (0 to $089F-1), adds the filter sweep step $08BC/$08BD to the cutoff shadow $0962/$0963, then for each voice X = 2 down to the limit in $045E (Y = its SID register offset from $0943): steps the voice's divider $08E6/$08E9 and arpeggio phase $08D7; on a tempo tick reads commands from the voice's data pointer ($FC/$FD from $0940/$093D) and calls each through the handler tables $0966/$098B (patching the JSR at $03D5) until a note; then per frame applies slide ($076D), vibrato ($06A8), waveform table ($0948), arpeggio ($0679) and pulse sweep ($0623), and on a tempo tick counts the note down ($0464).
JSR operand patched by $03C3-$03CC with the command handler's address
Operand of the JSR at $03D5, written by $03C3-$03CC with the music command handler's address (from $0966/$098B) before each command is run; the rest of the voice loop follows.
High byte of the handler JSR's operand at $03D5, written by $03C9; after the handler, the pointer steps on ($0800) and the per-frame effects follow.

A symbol only because the clearing loop at $C000 (outside this range; the protection jumps there at $44B2 after a third wrong code) names $040A in its STA and steps that operand upward: here the middle of the music driver's voice loop.

Offset byte of the BNE at $040D in the music driver's waveform-table test (alternating modes: an odd divider step keeps the note's own waveform); named only because data bytes at $100C and $B103 happen to decode as ASL $040E.
Operand of CPX #$FF at $045D, patched by $1298: the voice loop's limit; 0 plays voices 2, 1 and 0, 1 plays 2 and 1, 2 plays voice 2 only. The loop's next pass or exit follows.
operand patched by $1298, the voice loop's limit: 0 plays voices 2, 1 and 0; 1 plays 2 and 1; 2 plays voice 2 only

Counts the voice's note length down ($093A low, $08EF high). When fewer than $08AD ticks remain it clears the gate bit of the voice's control shadow (release); at zero it starts the next note at $048A: resets the voice's counters, reloads AD, SR, pulse width and the vibrato delay, reads the note byte (0 = rest) and the length byte, works out the note's frequency and its two arpeggio partners ($08DD, $08DA intervals), writes control $090D, and takes a following ($19, n) pair as the length's high byte.

Middle of the new-note code ($048A): reads the note's length byte into $093A, steps past the note, loads the voice's waveform $090D into the control shadow and $08AA, and takes a ($19, n) pair as the length's high byte. ($5A00 in the land names this address only by coincidence of bytes.)
BIT abs hides LDA #$00 at $0529: entered at $0529 when no ($19, n) pair follows, so the length high byte is 0

Body of the tune start ($080C): clears the driver's variables $089E-$0938 (Y = $9B down to 1), sets each voice's release point $08AD to 2, length to 1 and vibrato period $0937 to 1, tempo $089F to 1; keeps the tune base in $0946/$0947; voice 0 reads from base+4, voices 1 and 2 from base+4 plus the 16-bit offsets in the tune's first four bytes ($056C-$0582, X = $7E and $7F). Sets $033C, silences ($0596) and runs two frames of the driver ($0880) to prime it.
Opcode byte of the first priming JSR $0880 in the tune start; $12C1 writes $20 (JSR) or $60 (RTS, so the start returns here without priming).
opcode patched by $12C1: $20 (JSR, prime the driver) or $60 (RTS, return at once)
Stops the tune: $033C = 0, then falls into $0596.
Clears the SID shadow $094D-$0964 and writes 0 to $D418 (volume off). $12C4 can turn the STA at $05A0 into an RTS so the volume is left alone.
Opcode of the STA $D418 in $0596; $12C4 writes $8D (silence the volume) or $60 (RTS, leave the volume alone).
opcode patched by $12C4: $8D (write volume 0) or $60 (skip)

Music command $10: end of a repeat (outer level). Counts the voice's repeat counter $0919 up; while it is below the argument, jumps the data pointer back to the mark saved by command $11 ($091F/$0925).
Music command $11: marks the start of a repeat (outer level): saves the voice's data pointer in $091F/$0925 and zeroes its counter $0919.
Music command $12: end of a repeat at the inner level (the same as $05A4 with the voice index plus 3).
Music command $13: start of a repeat at the inner level (as $05C0, index plus 3).
Music command $14: sets the voice's transpose $0901 (semitones added to every note).
Music command $05: an argument of 100 or more sets the release point $08AD (arg - 100 ticks before the note's end); below 100 it sets how many ticks the waveform table applies, $08B6.

Music command $07: an argument of $63 or more chooses the voice whose new notes restart the filter sweep ($089E = arg - 100); below, it sets the voice's waveform-table mode $08B3 (0 off, 1-5 a fixed entry for the first ticks, 6-10 alternating with the note's own waveform).

Music command $15: the argument's high nibble is the pulse-width sweep's upper bound $08FB (it rises while the pulse width high byte is below it, $0652), its low nibble the lower bound $08FE (it falls while at or above it, $0646).
Music command $16: vibrato half-period $0937 in frames.
Music command $17: SID resonance and filter routing shadow $0964 ($D417).
Music command $18: the cutoff high byte $08BE a new note on the filter voice restarts the sweep from.
Music command $1B: adds the argument to the mode/volume shadow $0965 ($D418).

Pulse-width sweep for voice X (Y = its SID offset), on frames where the divider $08E6 is 0: adds the step $0916 to the pulse width shadow $094F/$0950; with bounds set ($08FB nonzero) it bounces between $08FB and $08FE, direction in $08F8.
Music command $03: the voice's control byte (waveform and gate) for its notes, $090D.

Arpeggio for voice X: mode 1 ($08B0) alternates the note and its first partner ($08C2/$08C5) on each divider step; other modes cycle note, first partner, second partner ($08E3/$08E0) by the phase $08D7. Writes the frequency shadow.
Vibrato for voice X: after the delay $08D1 runs out, adds or subtracts the depth $08CE to the frequency every frame, in four phases ($08F5) of $0937 frames each.
Music command $1C: semitones from the note to the arpeggio's second partner, $08DD.
Music command $1D: filter sweep step: argument / 8 to $08BD (cutoff high), argument AND 7 to $08BC (cutoff low bits).
Music command $25: frames per tempo tick, $089F.
Music command $1F: semitones from the note to the arpeggio's first partner (also the slide target), $08DA.
Music command $19: does nothing when met as a command; after a note, a ($19, n) pair is read by $051A as the length's high byte.
Music command $1A: adds the argument to the voice's transpose $0901.
Music command $21: frames before the vibrato starts on each note, $08D4.
Music command $24: returns from a sub-sequence: the data pointer goes back to the call saved in $092B/$0931, the second level moves up, and the pointer steps past the 4-byte call.
Music command $20: a value added to the low byte of every frequency the voice looks up, $08EC.
Adds the vibrato depth $08CE to the voice's frequency $08A1/$08A4 and its shadow.
Subtracts the vibrato depth $08CE from the voice's frequency and its shadow.
Frequency of note A (bit 7 ignored) plus the voice's transpose $0901, from the table at $09B0, plus the detune $08EC: returns A = low byte, Y = high byte.
Music command $0C: slide step high byte $0907.

Slide for voice X, mode A ($08BF): 1 glides toward the first partner's frequency $08C2/$08C5 and stops on it, 2 slides up and 3 down by the step $0904/$0907 every frame. Runs only once the note is $08C8 ticks old.
Music command $0E: pulse-width sweep step $0916.
Advances the voice's data pointer $FC/$FD by one command (2 bytes).
Starts a tune: Y/X = the tune's address (low/high). Turns the driver off ($033C = 0) while $052F sets it up.
Music command $09: ticks into a note before the slide starts, $08C8.
Music command $0B: vibrato depth $08CE (0 = no vibrato).
Music command $0F: slide mode $08BF (0 off, 1 glide to partner, 2 up, 3 down).
Music command $08: arpeggio mode $08B0 (0 off, 1 two-note, other three-note).
Music command $06: the voice's divider $08B9, frames per step of the arpeggio and pulse sweep.
Music command $02: attack/decay for the voice's notes, $0913.
Music command $01: mode/volume shadow $0965 ($D418).
Music command $22: sets the slide target ($08C2/$08C5) to the frequency of the argument's note.

Music command $23: calls a sub-sequence at the tune base plus the 16-bit offset in the argument and the next byte; the caller's pointer is saved in $092B/$0931 (the previous one moves to $092E/$0934, two levels), then reading continues at the target ($03B7).
Music command $0A: sustain/release for the voice's notes, $090A.
Music command $1E: ends the tune: $0591 stops and silences, then drops two return addresses so the driver returns straight to $087B's caller.

The music driver's frame entry, called once a frame: returns at once when $033C is 0, else runs $033D and copies the SID shadow $094D-$0965 to $D400-$D418, from register $18 down to the limit at $088F (0 for all voices).
The driver's frame without the on/off test: runs $033D, then copies the shadow registers to the SID. Entered from $087B, and called twice by the tune start to prime the voices.
Operand of LDY #$18 at $0883: the first SID register copied, written by $129B ($18 in every set-up).
operand patched by $129B: first register copied ($18)
Operand of CPY #$FF at $088E: the lowest SID register copied, written by $129E (0, 7 or $0E).
operand patched by $129E: lowest SID register copied (0, 7 or $0E: leaves the voices the sound effects own alone)
Music command $0D: slide step low byte $0904.
Music command $04: pulse width high byte each note starts with, $0910.
RTS of music command $04 ($089A). The clear loop in $052F starts at $089D+1, so this byte is never cleared.
Voice whose new notes restart the filter sweep ($04A2), set by command $07 with an argument of 99 ($63) or more (argument - 100; 99 gives $FF, no voice).
Frames per tempo tick (command $25); 1 after $052F.
Frame counter within the tempo tick, 0 to $089F-1 ($033D); commands are read and lengths counted when it is 0.
Per voice (3 bytes): the voice's current frequency, low byte; with $08A4 the value slides and vibrato move.
Per voice: current frequency, high byte.
Per voice: the note playing, 0 for a rest.
Per voice: the note's control byte (waveform), restored by the waveform table code ($0432).
Per voice: ticks before a note's end at which the gate is cleared ($047C); 2 after init.
Per voice: arpeggio mode (command $08).

Per voice: waveform-table mode (command $07): 0 off, 1-5 entry $0948+n-1 from the note's second tick to tick $08B6 (the first tick, age 0, keeps the note's own waveform, $041B), 6 and up alternate entry n-5 with the note's waveform.
Per voice: how many ticks the waveform table applies (0 = the whole note).
Per voice: frames per divider step (command $06).
Filter sweep step, cutoff low bits (0-7), command $1D.
Filter sweep step, cutoff high byte, command $1D.
Cutoff high byte the sweep restarts from (command $18).
Per voice: slide mode (command $0F).
$08BF+1, the base $052F uses with X = $7E-$7F to write voice 1 and 2's data pointer high bytes ($093E, $093F).

Per voice: frequency high byte of the arpeggio's first partner, also the glide target ($0834). (The auto label at $08C0 is $08BF+1: $052F indexes from $08C0 and $08C3 with X = $7E-$7F to reach the voice pointers at $093E/$0941.)
$08C2+1, the base $052F uses with X = $7E-$7F to write voice 1 and 2's data pointer low bytes ($0941, $0942).
Per voice: first partner's frequency, low byte.
Per voice: ticks before the slide starts (command $09).
Per voice: tempo ticks since the note started.
Per voice: vibrato depth (command $0B).
Per voice: frames left before the vibrato starts, reloaded from $08D4 at each note.
Per voice: vibrato delay (command $21).
Per voice: three-note arpeggio phase 0-2, stepped with the divider.
Per voice: semitones to the first partner (command $1F).
Per voice: semitones to the second partner (command $1C).
Per voice: second partner's frequency, low byte. Nothing writes it but the clear in $052F: $04DB stores only the high byte (TYA), so the second partner always has low byte 0.
Per voice: second partner's frequency, high byte ($04DF).
Per voice: frame counter within the divider step.
Per voice: divider steps counted; bit 0 alternates the two-note arpeggio and the waveform table.
Per voice: added to every looked-up frequency's low byte (command $20).

Per voice: note length, high byte (a ($19, n) pair after a note, $052B; 0 at init, $0542). The countdown's borrow ($046F) takes it to $FF when a length of 0 is counted past zero; while it holds $FF, $03A8 reads commands on every tempo tick.
Per voice: frames into the current vibrato phase.
Per voice: vibrato phase 0-3 (1 and 2 subtract, 0 and 3 add).
Per voice: pulse sweep direction, 1 = down.
Per voice: pulse sweep upper bound, pulse width high byte (command $15's high nibble): $0623 adds the step while the high byte is below it; 0 means no bounds.
Per voice: pulse sweep lower bound (command $15's low nibble): going down, $0623 turns back up once the high byte is below it; going up, it turns down at or above it.
Per voice: transpose in semitones (commands $14 and $1A).
Per voice: slide step, low byte (command $0D).
Per voice: slide step, high byte (command $0C).
Per voice: SR value for new notes (command $0A).
Per voice: control byte for new notes (command $03).
Per voice: pulse width high byte for new notes (command $04).
Per voice: AD value for new notes (command $02).
Per voice: pulse sweep step (command $0E).
Repeat counters, 6 bytes: voice X at $0919+X (outer) and $091C+X (inner).
Repeat marks, data pointer low byte, 6 bytes (outer, then inner level).
Repeat marks, data pointer high byte, 6 bytes.
Sub-sequence return pointer, low byte, per voice; $092E holds the second level.
Second-level return pointer, low byte, per voice.
Sub-sequence return pointer, high byte, per voice.
Second-level return pointer, high byte, per voice.
Per voice: vibrato half-period in frames (command $16), 1 after init.
Per voice: note length countdown, low byte.
Per voice: data pointer, high byte.
Per voice: data pointer, low byte.
SID register offset of each voice: 0, 7, 14.
The tune's base address, low byte; sub-sequence offsets are added to it ($085E).
The tune's base address, high byte ($0560). Also index 0 of the waveform table read as $0947+n ($042D), never used since n starts at 1.
Waveform table, 5 control bytes ($41 pulse, $21 saw, $11 triangle, $81 noise, $51 pulse+triangle, all with gate), used by the waveform-table modes ($042D). Not cleared by $052F.

The music's copy of the SID registers $D400-$D418 (25 bytes): three voices of 7 bytes, then $0962 cutoff low, $0963 cutoff high, $0964 resonance/routing, $0965 mode/volume. $087B copies it to the chip each frame.
Shadow of $D401 and on, as addressed by voice offset Y: $094E+Y frequency high, $094F+Y pulse low, $0950+Y pulse high, $0951+Y control, $0952+Y AD, $0953+Y SR.
Shadow of the pulse width low byte of the voice at offset Y ($094F+Y), moved by the pulse sweep $0623.
Shadow of the pulse width high byte of the voice at offset Y ($0950+Y), set at each new note from $0910 and moved by the pulse sweep.
Shadow of the control register (waveform and gate) of the voice at offset Y ($0951+Y): from $090D at each note, the waveform table ($0437) and the release ($0486).
Shadow of the attack/decay register of the voice at offset Y ($0952+Y), from $0913 at each note.
Shadow of the sustain/release register of the voice at offset Y ($0953+Y), from $090A at each note.
Shadow of $D415, the filter cutoff low bits, moved by the filter sweep ($034E).
Shadow of $D416, the filter cutoff high byte, moved by the filter sweep and reset per note on the filter voice ($04AD).
Shadow of $D417, resonance and filter routing (command $17).
Shadow of $D418, filter mode and volume (commands $01 and $1B).
Music command handlers, low bytes: entry n is command n+1 (a command is a byte 1-$25 followed by an argument byte).
Music command handlers, high bytes, matching $0966.
SID frequency of each of 96 notes, low byte then high byte, 8 octaves ($0106 for the lowest, $F810 for the highest), read by $0751.
High bytes of the note frequencies, interleaved with the low bytes at $09B0 (read as $09B1,Y by $0761).
Notes 32-63 of the music driver's frequency table (from $09B0): low byte, then high byte, of each SID frequency, read through $09B0,Y and $09B1,Y by $0751-$0761.
Notes 64-95, the top third of the music driver's frequency table (from $09B0), low then high byte; the last pair, at $0A6E, is the highest note the driver can play.

The sound-effect player's frame entry (called by $1178 and through $BC9C after $BC9F has started any requested effects): for each effect channel Y = 2 down to 0 (the start value at $0A71 is patched by $12A2 to use 3, 2 or 1 channels) whose block ($0C7C) is active ($0C3A), counts down the layer-alternation timer ($0C3E, reloaded from $0C34, flipping $0C3B), then runs $0A9F with the channel's SID voice offset ($0C79) in $FF.
Operand of the LDY at $0A70: the highest effect channel played, patched by $12A2 (2, 1 or 0); then the per-channel loop.
operand patched by $12A2: the highest effect channel played (2, 1 or 0)
operand is the loop counter, stored by $0A72 each pass
Operand of LDY #$FF at $0A99: the effect channel being played, stored by $0A72 each pass so the loop can count down.

One frame of an effect on channel Y (block offset X, SID offset in $FF): counts the duration $0C32/$0C35 down (a negative high byte never ends); at the end marks the channel free ($0C3A and the priority $1B82,Y to 0) and silences the voice's control, AD and SR. Otherwise sweeps layer A's pulse width ($0C3C/$0C28, flag bit 0) and layer B's ($0C3D/$0C2E, flag bits 3 and 4) down by $0C2F, sweeps layer A's frequency ($0C36/$0C37) and layer B's ($0C38/$0C39) by their steps between their bounds, applying the end-of-sweep action in the mode byte $0C33 (stop, restart at the far bound, or reverse), and writes frequency, pulse and control of layer A, or of layer B when the flags' bit 3 is set and the toggle $0C3B is 1.
Operand of LDA #$FF at $0B5D: written by $0B3D with the bound a sweep wraps to; the rest of the frequency sweeps and the register writes follow.
operand patched by $0B3D: the frequency high byte a sweep restarts from
Operand of LDA #$FF at $0BCD: layer B's wrap value, written by $0BAD.
operand patched by $0BAD: layer B's restart frequency high byte

Effect channel blocks: three of 29 bytes at $0C22, $0C3F and $0C5C (offsets 0, $1D, $3A in $0C7C); the labels $0C22-$0C3E name the fields of channel 0's block, indexed by X. Byte 0: attack/decay. Bytes 0-19 are copied from the effect definition by $0C84, bytes 20-28 are run-time state.
Field 1: sustain/release.
Field 2: layer A's lower frequency bound (high byte); the start frequency when sweeping up.
Field 3: layer A's upper frequency bound (high byte); the start when sweeping down.
Field 4: layer A's frequency step per frame, low byte.
Field 5: layer A's frequency step, high byte.
Field 6: layer A's pulse width high byte, decremented as the low byte $0C3C sweeps down.
Field 7: bit 0 sweeps layer A's pulse width; bit 3 enables the second layer B (and its frequency sweep); bit 4 with bit 3 sweeps layer B's pulse width.
Field 8: layer B's lower frequency bound (high byte).
Field 9: layer B's upper frequency bound.
Field 10: layer B's frequency step, low byte.
Field 11: layer B's frequency step, high byte.
Field 12: layer B's pulse width high byte.
Field 13: pulse width step per frame (both layers).
Field 14: layer A's control byte (waveform and gate).
Field 15: layer B's control byte.
Field 16: duration countdown, low byte.

Field 17: sweep mode. Bits 0-1 layer A's direction (0 none, 1 up, 2 or 3 down); bits 2-3 what happens at a bound (0 stop, 4 restart from the other bound, 8 or 12 reverse by EOR 3, which turns 1 and 2 into each other but 3 into 0, a stop); bits 4-5 and 6-7 the same for layer B.
Field 18: frames between switches of layer A and B ($0A82).
Field 19: duration countdown, high byte; bit 7 set = endless.
Field 20 (state): layer A's frequency, low byte (0 at the start).
Field 21 (state): layer A's frequency, high byte.
Field 22 (state): layer B's frequency, low byte.
Field 23 (state): layer B's frequency, high byte.
Field 24 (state): 1 while the channel plays an effect.
Field 25 (state): which layer sounds, 0 = A, 1 = B.
Field 26 (state): layer A's pulse width, low byte.
Field 27 (state): layer B's pulse width, low byte.
Field 28 (state): frames left before the layers switch.
Effect channel 1's 29-byte block (same fields as $0C22-$0C3E). Its bytes as loaded are not an effect; $0C84 overwrites them before use.
Effect channel 2's 29-byte block (same fields as $0C22-$0C3E).
SID register offset of each effect channel's voice: 0, 7, 14 (voices 1, 2, 3).
Offset of each channel's block from $0C22: 0, $1D, $3A.
Offset of the last copied byte of each channel's block ($13, $30, $4D), where $0C84's backwards copy starts; $0C82-$0C83 ($FF $FF) are not read.

Starts effect Y on channel X (called by $BC9F-$BCCF for each requested channel): copies the effect's 20-byte definition, addressed through the table at $C144/$C145, into the channel block; hard-restarts the voice (control $08 then 0, AD/SR 0), clears the run-time state, marks the channel active, sets AD/SR and the alternation timer, and starts each layer's frequency at its lower bound, or its upper bound when it sweeps down.
Operand of LDA $FFFF,Y at $0C9C: the effect definition's address, written by $0C91/$0C97 from the table at $C144; the hard restart and set-up follow.
operand patched with the effect definition's address
High byte of the effect definition's address in the LDA at $0C9C, written by $0C97.
Operand of LDY #$FF at $0CA7: the channel number, written by $0C84.
operand patched by $0C84: the channel number

Silences the SID: zeroes $D417 down to $D401 (the loop stops before $D400 and never touches $D418), and clears the sound requests $1B85-$1B8A. Called on pause ($2273), level end and loading ($3B6B, $3D8F, $3EC5, $CBB3).
Sound effect definition 0 (20 bytes at $0D2E, effect 0 of 35 in the table at $C144): all zero, a silent effect; used by sound 0.

High byte of the dispatcher's exit JMP at $1881, written by $1840 from the operand at $183F.
Makes the next $1809 point the dispatcher's exit jump ($1881) at $1803, the game's own register restore, for when the KERNAL is switched out: writes $03/$18 into the operands at $183A/$183F.
Makes the next $1809 point the dispatcher's exit jump back at the KERNAL's $EA7E (operands $183A/$183F = $7E/$EA).

Front-end raster routine (called from the game-over screen's interrupt handlers $3EE0, $3EEF and the ending's $D63F): waits in the NOP slide ($B1A1), then for each raster line Y = 0 to the count at $18BC less one writes one colour from the table chosen by $193A ($10xx + Y, the low byte at $18A8) to $D021 and to the register at $18AE/$18AF ($D020, or the dummy byte $18C0); every line but each eighth (Y AND 7 = 0) is padded with a delay so a colour lasts one raster line.
The line loop of $189A: one colour per raster line from the patched table into $D021 and the second register.
Low byte of the LDA $10FF,Y at $18A7: the raster-bar colour table, written by $193A from $195D.
operand patched by $193A from $195D: low byte of the colour table ($10xx)
Low byte of the STA $FFFF at $18AD: the bars' second register, $20 ($D020) or $C0 ($18C0), written by $1959.
operand patched by $1956/$1959: the second register written, $D020 or $18C0
High byte of the bars' second store at $18AD: $D0 or $18, written by $1956.
Operand of CPY #$FF at $18BB: the number of raster-bar lines, written by $1943 from $1962.
operand patched by $193A from $1962: number of lines
A spare byte: $193A points the bar routine's second store here when the border is to be left alone.

Raster handler: next link $22E9 at line $FA; $18D3 waits in the NOP slide, turns extended colour mode on ($19C2), places sprites 3 and 4 and colours sprites 0-5 white, sets the sprite pointers at $47FA/$4BFA and $47FE-$47FF/$4BFE-$4BFF, and clears X expansion and the background colours $D021-$D023.

The bottom panel's raster work for $18C1: waits in the NOP slide (entered at $B1A4, low byte patched by $22E3 from $3483 to follow sprite 7's height), turns extended colour mode on, places sprites 3 and 4 at X $8E and $E7, colours sprites 0-5 white, sets sprite pointers ($47FA/$4BFA = 2, $47FE-$47FF/$4BFE-$4BFF = $0F), clears X expansion and the colours $D021-$D023 (the STX at $1917 is turned into an RTS, $60, by $F328).
Operand of the JSR at $18D3 into the NOP slide: its low byte is written each frame by $22E3 from the table at $3483, so the panel's split follows sprite 7's height; the panel set-up follows.
Entry used by $F413: the panel set-up from the sprite placement on, without the NOP-slide wait or the extended colour switch.
Operand of LDA #$01 at $18E3: sprite 3's colour on the panel, written by $1C15 and $36BF (1), and by $F0E1 (from $EFE5+X, in the sad land while $36F3 is set).
Operand of LDA #$01 at $18E8: sprite 4's colour on the panel, written by $1C12 (1) and by $F0D1 (from $EFD3+X or $EFDC+X while $1BB8 is set).
Operand of LDA #$01 at $18ED: sprite 5's colour on the panel, written by $1C0F and $3883 (1), and by $F0BD (from $EFEE+X while $1BB7 is set).
Opcode of the STX $D021 at $1917 in the panel routine: STX, or RTS ($60, written by $F328) to keep the panel's background colours.
opcode patched by $F328 ($60 RTS): the panel then keeps its background colours

A 25-byte scratch area $1921-$1939 shared by several routines: the level reveal keeps zero page $83-$8D here ($11B2) and $4B-$4E at $192C; $13E7 keeps each row's lost first character from $1921; $BBEB uses $1921/$1922 for a multiplication; $F181 copies 25 bytes from $1921 to ($50).
Second byte of the scratch area: the high byte of $BBEB's multiplication.
$192C-$192F: the level reveal's copy of zero page $4B-$4E (colour RAM pointers), saved at $11BC and restored at $11FE.
The value of $20F3 kept by $1100 during the level reveal and restored at $1189.
$1931-$1939: the end of the scratch area ($F181 copies up to $1939).

Chooses one of five raster-bar set-ups X = 0-4 for $189A: colour table low byte from $195D ($1030, $1040, $1040, $1071, $1068), line count from $1962 ($10, $10, $FF, $10, $09), and whether the border is coloured too ($1967 nonzero: $D020, else $18C0). Called by $3ED6, $3EE5 (the game-over screen's raster chain) and $D632, $D64A (ending).
Raster-bar set-ups 0-4: low byte of the colour table at $10xx. $1961 (set-up 4) is rewritten by $D62D and stepped by $D642/$D645 to move the bars.
Raster-bar set-ups 0-4: number of lines.
Raster-bar set-ups 0-4: nonzero colours the border as well (set-up 2).

Start-up. Switches the BASIC and KERNAL ROMs out ($01 = $35), keeps the current raster line in $1B42, calls $BBA6, writes $C1 into the low byte of the NMI vector at $0318, selects VIC bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF) through CIA 2 port A, sets screen $4400 and characters $7800 ($19AA), sets the CIA 1 port directions for the keyboard and stick ($19A0), runs $3F52, then jumps to the protection screen at $4400.
CIA 1 port B as input, port A as output.
$D018 = $1F: screen $4400, characters $7800 in bank 1.
$D018 = $2F: screen $4800, characters $7800 in bank 1.
Clears $D011 bit 6, extended colour mode.
Disables every sprite, then sets extended colour mode ($19C2).
Sets $D011 bit 6, extended colour mode.
Clears $D011 bit 4, blanking the screen.
Sets $D016 bit 4, multicolour mode.
Background black ($D021 = 0), then falls into $19E2 (multicolour off). Called by $F241 and the stage card's raster handler $3DA5.
Clears $D016 bit 4.
Clears the low four bits of $D016: 38 columns, horizontal scroll 0. No caller found.
$D016 with the fine scroll 0 and 40 columns (bit 3).
Fills $43C0-$43FE with A.
Zeroes the X and Y position registers of sprites 0-7, $D000-$D00F (X = $0F down to 0); the X high bits in $D010 are left as they are. Called at $1D49, $4465 and $45A5.
Background and border black.

Fills the colour RAM with A and both screens with X (each stored into the operand of a load in the loop first): four bands each, X = $FB down to 1, cover $D800-$DBE8, $4400-$47E8 and $4800-$4BE8, one byte past each 1000-byte area.
Operand of LDA #$FF at $1A24: the colour fill value, written by $1A1F; the colour RAM half of the fill loop.
Operand of LDA #$FF at $1A32: the screen fill value, written by $1A1C.
Switches to $01 = $35: RAM everywhere but the I/O chips. $1A51 is the same without the SEI.
Sets the sprite chip's shared registers (multicolours $D025/$D026, priority, multicolour mode, X and Y expansion, X high bits, enable) from eight six-entry tables at $1A87-$1AB1, entry X.
Sprite set-ups 0-5 for $1A56, multicolour 1 ($D025) of each.
Sprite set-ups 0-5: multicolour 2 ($D026).
Sprite set-ups 0-5: sprite-behind-background bits ($D01B).
Sprite set-ups 0-5: multicolour mode bits ($D01C).
Sprite set-ups 0-5: X expansion bits ($D01D).
Sprite set-ups 0-5: Y expansion bits ($D017).
Sprite set-ups 0-5: X position high bits ($D010).
Sprite set-ups 0-5: sprite enable bits ($D015).

Reads joystick port 2 ($DC00) once and spreads its five bits over $1BDE-$1BE2 (up, down, left, right, fire): each byte keeps only its own bit, so 0 means pressed. The value read lands in the operand at $1AC5, the mask in $1AC7.
Operand of LDA #$FF at $1AC4: the joystick byte read from $DC00 by $1AB7; $1AC7 holds the mask for each direction in turn.
Operand of AND #$FF at $1AC6: the direction mask, $10 first and halved for each of the five directions.
Writes A to $DC00 to select keyboard rows, returns the column bits from $DC01 once two reads agree, then deselects ($1AE1).
Writes $7F to both CIA 1 ports.
Low bytes of the 25 row addresses of a 40-column screen (0, $28, ... $C0), read by $2A93 with $1B03 to point $8A/$8B at a row of screen $4400.
High bytes of the 25 row addresses of screen $4400 ($44-$47), read by $2A9B; $2AA8 adds $3481 to reach the shown screen.
Entry 3 of the screen row high bytes ($44), read through $2A9B's LDA $1B03,Y like the others. The bytes AE 06 1B at $FF82 that look like LDX $1B06 are inside the happy tune's data, not code.
Inverts every byte of $7800-$7FFF (EOR #$FF), the character set's 2 KB.
The RTS of invert_7800. Also the base of $1BF3's clear loop (STA $1B39,X with X = $8F down to 1 clears $1B3A-$1BC8).

Which screen is shown: 1 = $4400 ($D018 = $1F), 0 = $4800 ($2F). Set to 1 at the level start ($1CA2), flipped with the $D018 operand $21AA by $2667 when the screens swap; indexes $29A5 (the shown screen's page) and $3481. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Set to 1 by the raster interrupt each frame ($2088); the play loop at $1E9B waits for it and decrements it, so a pass of the game runs at most once a frame. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Character columns the scroll has passed and the map scroller has not drawn yet: raised by the scroll step in the interrupt ($20D1), taken one at a time by the play loop ($1F27, which then draws a column) and by the level start's scroll-in ($1CE3). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Written by $3E65 and incremented at $BE4F; read by $3E6A, $BE8C, $BF67, $D53A and $D624. Its meaning is not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Set to 3 by $2554 when a pass has swapped the screens and recoloured a column; while it is set the play loop skips the game's work for that pass ($1F51-$200C) and the band-4 handler skips $F07E. Cleared at the end of each pass ($2065) and by the scroll-in ($1D01). The scroll-in at the level start ($1CFA) waits for it. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Direction of travel and scroll: 0 = right (the map moves left, coarse column $0F counts up), nonzero = left. Written when the player turns ($3202, $3245); read by the scroll step ($2093), the map scroller, the player's wall tests and much of the object code. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
1 after the coarse column last wrapped while scrolling left ($2985), 0 after a wrap scrolling right ($253D); read by $2444 for where the new column goes and copied into $1B42 by $3205.

Set to 1 by $31FC when the player turns left, written by $3242, cleared by $267A at each wrap; with $1B40 it moves the new column's screen address by 40 ($2442, $245A, $28AC). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

When nonzero, $2550 colours a second, neighbouring column; cleared there ($25EC). Start-up leaves the raster line in it ($1972); $320A copies $1B40 into it. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Direction of the hidden screen's one-character shift ($1395): 0 left ($13E7), 1 right ($1435); flipped when a shift finishes; also read by $3923, $3934, $F197. Cleared by $2678. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Flipped by $13C6 after shifts; read by $2463, $28BF and $F15B to adjust the new column's position. Cleared by $2678. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Set to 1 by $13C3 the first time a shift completes in direction 0; while set, each completed shift also flips $1B44 ($13AA). Cleared by $2678. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Passes of the one-character shift of the hidden screen still to do: 6 written by $3214/$3263 when the player turns, counted down by $1395; while nonzero the play loop skips $38C4 ($1F67) and $315E branches. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Cleared when the player stops ($2C93); written by $32D3 and $32E1, read by $3166. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Set by the scroll step ($20AC, $20CA) when the coarse column wraps past 0 or 39; the map scroller then swaps the screens and moves the colour RAM ($2471, $28D2) and clears it ($254D, $2992). The frame-end handler ($22F5, $230C) and $2A5C read it. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Which edge started the current map repeat: 1 ($27CC, a $D0-$DF marker), $FF ($27D7, an $E0-$EF marker), 0 none ($27A5). Set from the land's table at the level start ($1CC5). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Set by $F169 (when $1B44 is 0 and the screen column $1BDD is $28 or more), cleared by $F16F; while set, the play loop calls $F16D before scrolling right ($1F40). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

The player's height above his row on a slope, in pixels: set from the slope tables by $2FBE (slope glyphs $9081-$9084, $2EF9) and by $30D7 (slope characters $9088-$908B, $3012), cleared off a slope ($2FEE, $3107), when a jump starts from a slope ($2CF6, after folding it into Y, doubled first by $2CE7 when $1BB6 is set), by a forced bounce ($2EBD), by $B5F4 when the player is stopped (with $1B7F set) and at the level start ($1E02); subtracted from his Y ($1BE4) wherever the row is worked out ($2A3E, $33C5, $B2A3, ...). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

1 while the player's position is not inside the map: set each pass by $2B81, cleared by $2A45 once $2A3A has found his row. While set the floor and head tests are skipped and a fall goes on until he is out of the bottom ($2E80). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

$30 at the level start ($1DF8); written by $BE4C, $EEA8, $EF11, $EF8F, raised by $B22E, $D5CA, $D621, $F369; read by the code at $B1D3, $BE91-$BF0E, $D53F-$D5C1, $E4AF, $EF3F. Ducking changes it (features.md); its meaning is not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

$16 at the level start ($1DFD); evened down by $2C70 when the player stops; written by $3347, $33CF, $EF3B, raised by $D5B8; read by $D5A8, $EF14, $EF21. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

$E0 when the glyph at the player's middle is the land's $9025 or $9026, 0 for $9027 or $9028 ($2B3C); also written by $B34B and $B5FA. The band routines OR it into a value ($C063, $C0C3, $C11E) and $B4A8 reads it: by its value, the sprite-behind-background bits of sprites 5-7, so the player can pass behind scenery (inferred). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Written by $334A, $33CC, $EF2F; counted down at $EF24. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

The player's running speed: cleared when he stops ($2C4C); $5D is full speed ($2C33, where a wall at full speed causes a bump). Written by the run code at $31CB-$3374. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

$4C at the level start ($1E19), 0 from the walk-in ($2391); compared with A when the player stops ($2C7C: a difference plays sound 6), and read by $2E07, $32A9-$3380, $B5B9, $C6D7, $EECC. Written by $33D2, raised by $3342. Meaning not fully traced. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Written by $328E, $333D, $33D5, counted down at $3318, read by $3313. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Nonzero while the player brakes into a skid: raised by $31A5 and $2394, cleared when he stops ($2C90). In the finish stretch ($1BC6) each character skidded adds to the skid distance $1BF0/$1BF1 and plays sound $2C with a rising pitch ($1EFD-$1F24); $147A puffs dust behind a skid; read also by $32B7-$337B, $B5AA, $BE58, $BF1E, $EEBA. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Frames of the dust-puff effect still to start sprites ($147A): set by $F048 from A (3 after a wall bump, 2 after a long fall) and by $3357/$33DD/$E2F7; read by $2C26 and $33C9. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Dust-puff parameter set with $1B55 ($F04B, $3352, $E2F2), read also by $33D8. While it is set and $1B57 is clear (with $1BB6 = 0), a new puff starts at a fixed X position, $A4 or $B4 by the scroll direction ($1523-$1539), not at the player's X, and its Y gets no +4 ($1578). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Dust-puff parameter, from X in $F043 ($F04E): 0 or 1.

Cleared when a puff ends ($1501), written by $33E0 and $E2FA, read by $334D, $3388 and $F043 (which starts no new puff while it is set). With $1BB6 set and $208C not 0, a new puff starts at a fixed X position, $A0 or $B8 by the scroll direction, while it is 0 ($150C-$1521), and at the player's X while it is set. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Nonzero while the player rises in a jump: set by $2D74 and $2EC1 (and $B60E), cleared at the top or a head bump. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Nonzero while the player falls: set at the top of a jump, on walking off a ledge ($2D4E) and after a head bump; cleared on landing ($2E6D). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Rising or falling, as worked out by $2ACE each pass; picks the rows the wall tests use and is read by the effects ($1540, $1566), slopes and object code.
Set with $1B5F when up starts a jump on a slope ($2CFB); the next pass starts the jump at $2D62. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Index into the jump speed table at $3460 ($33A1, $33B3): $17 at the start of a jump, counted down while rising and up (to $1F) while falling; cut to 6 when up is released early. A forced bounce sets it from A ($2ECA). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Which way the stick asks the player to go: $FF left, 1 right, 0 none (written by $2BDF-$2C22, read by $31B6). features.md: right and left set it to $01 and $FF. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
1 while up has been held since the jump began; a new jump needs it 0 ($2CAB).
Set to 6 when a jump was cut short by releasing up ($2D9E), so the cut happens once; cleared at the top and on bumps. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Frames left of a drop through a platform (down and fire): set from $2CA9 by $2D20, counted down at $2AB9; while it runs only walls are solid. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
1 while down is held without fire on the ground ($2D2B); the wall tests then use the lower rows. features.md: down sets $1B62/$1B63.
Raised by $318E/$3198 and written by $31B0, read by $3189/$3193. Down changes it (features.md); meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Frame divider counted down by $BDD7 in the bottom raster handler, 5 to 0 and round: the play loop counts $1B79 only when it is 0 ($201E); read by $364F. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Frame divider, 4 to 0 and round ($BDE1).
Frame divider, 3 to 0 and round ($BDEB); read by $2DD9 (the floaty jump), $3F1E, $D5A3-$D616, $F364.
Frame divider, 2 to 0 and round ($BDF5); read by $B354, $BCD8, $BE12, $BEAE, $BEF7, $BF28, $F07E, $F36C.

Flips between 0 and 1 every frame ($BE04): halves the rate of the background flash ($20E5), the floaty jump ($2DD4), the colour cycles at $3EF4 and other paced work; when the scroll speed $1BD7 is below 2, the glyph rotation in $22E9 shifts one bit only on the frames where it is 1.
Effect sprites (two entries, X = 0, 1): X position, low byte. Started at the player's X ($1BE3) and moved against the scroll ($15D7, $15E7).
X position of effect sprite 1 ($147A compares the two).
Effect sprites: Y position ($1591), from the player's Y less the slope offset and $1478.
Y position of effect sprite 1 (written also by $BBA2). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Effect sprites: sprite pointer (animation frame); $0F means the entry is free. Shown through sprite 5 by $21DF.
Frame of effect sprite 1 ($0F when free).
Effect sprites: $20 when the X position has carried past 255 (sprite 5's bit in $D010), else 0.
X high flag of effect sprite 1.
While nonzero (set from $1474 by $3403) only effect sprite 0 is animated, and it counts down ($14AC). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Frames until the effect sprites' next animation step, reloaded from $1476. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Which effect sprite the extra raster handler shows ($21DF); written by $3413, $B2F3, $E45A. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

1 while the player stands on a slope glyph ($2FE9); read by the wall and jump code ($2C2B, $2C3E, $2CDD) and $2A69; $FF ($3102, from $3012) while he stands on one of the slope characters $9088-$908B: $2B6E then runs only $3012, not $2EF9.

The spinning star's pass counter: reloaded from $EE10 by $3AFB and counted down by the DEC $1B75 at $3AEE (an instruction whose opcode $B7C9 rewrites); when it goes negative the next star frame is shown. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Written by $3B17, raised by $F2AA, read by $3AFE and $BEDC. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Written by $3B0C, read by $3B04. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Read by $3521, $35F3, $361C and $3B86 (into $F322), written by $360C, $362D, $F323. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
A countdown taken by the play loop ($2028) on passes where $1B64 is 0, so every sixth frame; at 0 it runs $361C. Set by $3601 and $3626. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Written by $351E, $35EF; read by $350E. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Written by $36CE, $3791; read by $366D, $3707. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Written by $37D0, $37DF; read by $3801. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Passes the player has spent below the map ($2A4A); once nonzero $2A3A is no longer run ($2B84).

Raised when the player falls out of the bottom of the screen ($2E88); the play loop then skips the movement ($2AAF), and after $1B80 runs out ends the life ($1F95); read also by $316E. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
When set (by $B5E9) the play loop runs $BD5A instead of the player's movement and burns time in the NOP slide; the band-1 handler leaves $1BA9 alone ($21F1); read by $E471.
Frames before a lost life is handled: $28 after a fall into a pit ($2EB1), also set by $BD8F; at 0 the play loop jumps to $3B3F ($1F90-$1FAA). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Steps of the level start's walk-in: $4C at the start ($1E16), counted down by the frame-end handler while $1BC9 is set ($2377-$23A2: by one a frame down to $41, then by two, stopping at 0), each frame adding $CF18,X to the player's X. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Priority of the effect playing on channel 0-2 (3 bytes, 0 = free): set by $1352, cleared when an effect ends ($0AB9) and at the level start ($1E8C). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Channel 1's priority.
Channel 2's priority.
Start requests for channels 0-2 (3 bytes): set by $1352, taken by $BC9F-$BCC7, cleared by $0D1B. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Channel 1's start request.
Channel 2's start request.
Effect number to start on channels 0-2 (3 bytes, from $1322 by $1352), read by $BCA9-$BCCC; $1545 also checks channel 0's for effects $10 and 3.
Effect requested on channel 1.
Effect requested on channel 2.

Three colours of the current colour set: copied from the land's $9095 + 3n by $29EF ($2A0E-$2A18, Y = 0-2). The fade $B34F also writes here: for each of its four sequences ($1B8F-$1B92, X = 3 down to 0) it stores the sequence's current entry ($B39E) into $1B8B-$1B8E ($B383). With $1B92 they are the four sequence numbers of the fade $B34F ($B374, X = 3 down to 0): $B39E looks up entry $1B93 of each sequence, a positive entry goes to $1B8B+X ($B383), a negative one ends the sequence and is stored here ($B37E). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Second of the level-start colours.
Third of the level-start colours.

Read by $B389, $B3AA, written by $B391. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

From the land's $96E3 at the level start ($1D69).
From the land's $96E3, then $1BD2 plus the land's $96F8 ($1E55); read and written by $E5E9-$E656. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
From the land's $96E3, then $1BD3 plus a carry ($1E5D); read and written by $E5F3-$E64A. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
From the land's $96F1 at the level start ($1D87), read by $E68F.

Counted down at $37FD (the address of features.md's extra-time POKE) and read at $37F8; set by $CB4D. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Written by $B595, read by $C727. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Written by $E6E5, $E7E4, $ECB7, read by $E998, $ECB2. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Set to 1 by $E345 when, in the happy land, the player meets map glyph $60 or $61 ($23CA → $E2F0, which also splices the extra raster handler in); $23D8 acts on glyphs $62-$63 while it is set.
