Its game meaning (a power-up) is inferred, not proven. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Raised at $B61D (the address of features.md's invincibility POKE), written by $387F, read by $B5E4 and $F0B5. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Raised at $384F, written by $F387, read by $3B8C and $F0C0. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Written by $383C, raised by $BEA7, read by $37E9 and $BEBE. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Raised by $2EA8 when the player falls into a pit beside glyph $4C or $4E (sad land, $36F3 set); read by $1F9A (then the life ends with A = 0 to $3B3F) and $3B80. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
10 after the player bumps his head with $1B52 clear ($2E0E); counted down at $EEB5. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Six timers $1BBC-$1BC1 counted down by $F08E (X-indexed); individual ones are set to $1E by $3606, $3609, $36D4, $CB52, $364A, and all but $1BBE by $10C1. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Second of the six timers: set to $1E by $3609 and by $10C1's loop; zeroed by $1BF3.
Third of the six timers: nothing sets it (the loop at $10C1 skips it); only the clear $1BF3 writes it, with 0. $F08E counts it like the others.
Fourth of the six timers: set to $1E by $36D4 and by $10C1's loop; zeroed by $1BF3.
Fifth of the six timers: set to $1E by $CB52 and by $10C1's loop; zeroed by $1BF3.
Sixth of the six timers: set to $1E by $364A and by $10C1's loop; zeroed by $1BF3.
Written by $B622 and $EF4E, read by $21CB, $B5CF, $EF45. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

1 while the map column $1BD9 lies between one of the land's start columns ($902B-$902D) and end columns ($9031-$9033) ($F121, $F13E): the frame-end handler then rotates two glyphs of the character set ($2314). Also written by $1C80. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
No reader or writer found by address (cleared with the block by $1BF3).
1 while the game is paused (the RUN/STOP test in $2222); the play loop then only reads Q.

Set when the player crosses the finish line in the happy land ($2B5D); the play loop then counts $1BC7 down and ends the stage, the skid distance is counted, and the player no longer steers ($2B04). Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Passes from crossing the finish line to the stage's end: $6E at the level start ($1D5C), counted down at $2056; at 0 the play loop jumps to $3B3F with A = 1. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.
Written by $B5F7, raised by $BD69, read by $BD5F. Meaning not traced from this range. Also zeroed by $1BF3, the clear of $1B3A-$1BC8.

Nonzero while the game moves the player itself: $FF from $1BFE at the level start, 1 during the scroll-in and reveal ($1D0B), 0 in play ($1D2B). While set the scroll step does not raise the frame flag ($20D4), the frame-end handler walks the player in, marker tunes are not taken and the band-1 handler skips $BA08; its sign selects $B293 for the border ($2121).
Column within the tile (0-3) at the right screen edge: 3 at the level start ($1CA7), stepped by $23EE/$2858, written by $2648 and $28A6. $FF from $1BFE before that.
Column within the tile (0-3) at the left screen edge: 0 at the level start ($1CAC), stepped by $2439/$2858, read by $324E and $3A2E. $FF from $1BFE before that.
While nonzero the play loop sets the scroll speed $208C to 0 ($1EDB); set by $32D0/$32DE, cleared when the player stops ($2C8D). Set to $FF by $1BFE at the level start.
Filled with $FF by $1BFE; no other reader or writer found by address.
The raster band routine set in use (from $29B0); $FF after $1BFE so the first set is always applied.
The colour set in use (from $29EF); also written by $1DB1 at the level start. Set to $FF by $1BFE at the level start.
The last tune marker passed ($2A29); $FF after $1BFE.

When nonzero the play loop does not move the player ($1EC5), the pause key is not read ($2231) and the bottom handler runs $B312; raised by $B395, read by $B34F, $B62F. Meaning not traced from this range. Set to $FF by $1BFE at the level start.
Read at the level start ($1E4F, plus the land's $96F8 into $1BA5) and by $E5C9-$E692, written by $E5CE, $E5DD. Meaning not traced from this range. Set to $FF by $1BFE at the level start.
$7F at the level start ($1D7D), raised and lowered by $E5D3/$E5E2, compared at $E62C-$E686. Meaning not traced from this range. $FF from $1BFE just before.
Read by $E6BE, $E6DB, $ECBD, written by $E6E0, raised by $ECBA, $ECD5. Meaning not traced from this range. Set to $FF by $1BFE at the level start.
Written by $E6E8 and $ECD2; read by $B678, $C1C2, $C63B, $C8CD, $E7C1, $E962, $EC68. Meaning not traced from this range. Set to $FF by $1BFE at the level start.
While 0 the play loop runs $F1A5 (which sets it to $FF) before scrolling left ($1F2F); written by $F1A1. Set to $FF by $1BFE at the level start.

The scroll speed in pixels a frame, unsigned: the play loop turns it into the signed operand at $208C by the direction ($1EE5-$1EF5). Set by the run code ($32CB, $3377, $B5F1), by $2C66/$2C79 when the player stops, 8 during the scroll-in ($1CD3); kept in $1BD8 while paused. features.md lists it.
$1BD7 kept by the pause ($225E) and given back on resume ($2291).

Map column (0-255, in the band rows at $8A00-$8FFF) at the right edge of the screen; set at the level start ($1C83), stepped by the map scroller; read by $3A8D, $F121, $F13E. features.md's "position bytes" moved by +2/-2 in 40 frames of running.
Map column at the left edge of the screen: set at the level start nine tiles back from $1BD9 ($1C93), stepped by the scroller.
The right edge's repeat counter ($269F): 0 to the count, $FF when no repeat runs.
The left edge's repeat counter ($26E4).
The screen column (0-$27) where the next new map column is drawn: $27 at the level start, moved with every coarse step ($209D, $20B9) and turn ($31F7, $3256).
Joystick up, 0 when pressed ($1AB7). Read by the jump code ($2CD3, $2D8F).
Joystick down, 0 when pressed. Read by $2D09.
Joystick left, 0 when pressed. Read by $2B9C-$2C10 and $3E54.
Joystick right, 0 when pressed. Read by $2B97-$2C15 and $3E4B.
Fire button, 0 when pressed. Read by $2D0E (drop through), $332B, $3E5E.
The player's sprite X position: 2 at the level start ($1DD4), moved by the walk-in ($2381); read by $1553 and $B293.
The player's sprite Y position: from the land's $9714 at the level start; moved by the jump and fall code, snapped to rows ($CB7A) and steps; read widely.
The player's column offset from the start of his screen row, worked out by $2A3A.
The player's character row, ($1BE4 - $32)/8 ($2A57); stepped by $3128/$3140 on slope ends.
Written by $B609 and $EF42, read by $E4A6. Meaning not traced from this range.
10 at the level start ($1DEB); written by $BD05, $BD2C, $EF82; read by $E44F, $EF74. Meaning not traced from this range.
4 at the level start ($1DCD); read by $F0A4, $F0E5, written by $F0AC. Meaning not traced from this range.
$4A at the level start ($1D57), counted down at $37EE and written by $37F5. Meaning not traced from this range.
Read by $3326 and $C9BA, raised by $BC55, written by $E542. Meaning not traced from this range.

The land's state: 0 sad, 1 happy. $3B3F stores A here when a stage ends or restarts; the land's code at $A56C sets it. Chooses the title tune ($3C89), and only when it is set do the finish line ($2B42), the tune markers ($2A2C), the glyphs $60-$63 ($23AB) and the tune checks ($1FE3) act. 0 in the play snapshot at the start of Jellyland.
Counted down at $BE17 (the address features.md's unlimited-lives POKE guards) and reloaded by $BE31. Meaning not traced from this range.
Read by $BE21, added at $BE29, written by $BE2E. Meaning not traced from this range.
Characters skidded past the finish line ($1F07); read by $BE53, counted down by $BF51, written by $E571.
Tens digit of the skid distance ($1F14); read by the bonus code $BE68-$BF4E.
Units digit of the skid distance (0-9, $1F0B-$1F19).
Written only by $E571 (STA $1BEF,X with X = 3, clearing $1BEF-$1BF2 with the skid distance); no reader found.
Zeroes the play variables $1B3A-$1BC8 (STA $1B39,X for X = $8F down to 1). Called by the level start ($1D43), $3B92, $F2FF and the land's $A54F.
Sets $1BC9-$1BD6 to $FF (auto mode, and "nothing chosen yet" for the band set, colour set and tune marker). Called by the level start ($1D46) and the land's $A566.
Operand of LDA #$FF at $1BFE: the value $1BFE fills $1BC9-$1BD6 with. Nothing in the engine's code writes it: the bytes 8D FF 1B at $FFB7 (STA $1BFF) are leftovers that nothing executes.
Read and written by $E4F2, $E50F, $E574 (X/Y-indexed from $1C09). Meaning not traced from this range.
Written by $E514 and by $E574 (STA $1C09,X, X = 3 down to 0, with the value it puts in $1BEF-$1BF2); read by $E4F2 (copied to $51, Y = 3 down to 0).
Written by $EA9F and by $E574 (STA $1C09,X, X = 3 down to 0); read by $E4F2 (copied to $52).
Written by $EAA4 and by $E574 (STA $1C09,X, X = 3 down to 0); read by $E4F2 (copied to $53).
Writes 1 (white) into the operands of the panel's colour loads for sprites 5, 4 and 3 ($18EE, $18E9, $18E4) and returns X = 1. Called by $1C63 and $F31B.

Nonzero in play (5, set by the level start at $1D3A); the land's own sequence at $A549 (which also turns the land happy) writes 0. While 0 there are no sound effects in the reveal, the border takes its plain colour ($2114) and the frame-end handler skips its play work.

Blacks out for a level start: background and border black, $D011 = 0 (screen off), VIC interrupts off and acknowledged, fine scroll $10 = 0, both screens filled with the land's blank glyph ($9022) and colour RAM with 0, zero page $0B-$10 cleared (the raster save and both scroll positions), and the background flash counter $20E2 = 0.
The clear loop: STA $00,X for X = $0B to $10 (the label "start" shown as its operand is the zero-page base $00).

Installs the play-time raster chain: A/X/Y = the handler after the VSP interrupt and its line (into $2178, $217D, $2182), $FFFE/$FFFF = $22E9, NMI vector $FFFA/$FFFB = $2087 (the RTI of irq_leave, so RESTORE does nothing), $01 = $35, CIA 1 interrupts off, the panel sprites white ($1C0D), the raster interrupt on at line $FF, $D016 = $D8 (multicolour, 40 columns), CIA 1 timer A stopped, interrupts on.

Sets the map position for a level start: A into $1BC3, X = the map column at the right edge ($1BD9); counts nine tile columns back, skipping marker codes ($D0 and up), for the left edge ($1BDA); $D018 value $1F (screen $4400), screen column $27, shown screen 1, tile columns 3 and 0; and the playfield multicolours ($2108, $210D) from the land's $908F/$9091 for its state ($1BEC: sad or happy).

Sets the map repeat state for a level start: A = $1BDB, X = $1BDC, Y = $1B49 (from the land's $9730, $9737, $973E), and the second $D011 value of the VSP write ($219A) to $5B, extended colour with multicolour, a mode that shows black, so the playfield stays dark during the scroll-in.

The level start's scroll-in: speed 8 ($208C, $1BD7); each frame with a character passed ($1B3C) draws a new column ($23EE) and, in play ($1C19), moves the objects ($E72F, $E6BE) and sounds ($BC99, $BA0D); stops when the screens have swapped ($1B3E), with the speed back to 0 and $1BC9 = 1. Then $E5B4 (A = $AD in play, $60 otherwise), $E27B, CLC at $1FB2 (object updates off), the reveal ($1100) and $1BC9 = 0.

Starts or restarts a level (jumped to from $3DA2): resets the stack, blacks out ($1C1A), $1C19 = 5, $EFC4-$EFC9 = $11 (the X that $1C1A returns, through TXA), clears the play variables ($1BF3) and sets $1BC9-$1BD6 to $FF ($1BFE), parks the sprites, sets the skid sound's pitch ($0FD8 = 6), $BD96, $1BEA = $4A, $1BC7 = $6E, $1BA1-$1BA7 from the land's tables ($96E3, $96EA, $96F1), $1BD3 = $7F and $1BA8 = $80; the raster band set ($29B0, from $9706); the colour set ($9095, by $970D in the happy land, else $18); the raster chain ($1C3D: band 1 at line $52); the player's X 2 and Y ($9714), the reveal shape ($971B into $1155), $B34A ($9722), volume $0F; sprite registers; $C519, $33EB; the map position ($1C80 with the land's $9745 and $96FF); the background colour ($9093); the happy tune ($9729 into $1E77); $E5C8; the repeat state ($1CBF); the scroll-in ($1CCE); $1BA5/$1BA6; two sound-effect channels ($12A2), the music on voice 3 only ($128A) after starting the tune ($E4C5: tune 9 when sad, the land's choice when happy); then sounds $0B and $0C and falls into the play loop.

Operand of LDY #$00 at $1D5F: the restart point. The level start reads every per-start table in the land ($96E3-$9745: map column, player Y, colours, repeat state, tune) with this index; written by $B7BA, $E4ED, $E53F and $E563 and compared at $E4E8 (the active portal, by inference from features.md; not proven here).
Operand of LDY #$FF at $1E76: the happy land's first tune, written by $1E33 from the land's $9729.

The top of the play loop. Waits for the frame flag $1B3B and decrements it, deselects the keyboard ($1AE1). While paused ($1BC5) it only reads keyboard row 7 for Q (column 6): Q sets $CF81 to $FF and jumps to $3B3F with A = $1BEC. Otherwise reads the stick ($1AB7) and runs the pass.

The pass after the pause test: reads the stick; unless $1BD1 is set, moves the player ($2AAF, then $EE9E; or only $BD5A while $1B7F is set), and with $1BD1 set runs $EE9E alone; sets the signed scroll speed $208C from $1BD7 and the direction (0 while $1BCC is set); when a character has scrolled past ($1B3C) counts the skid distance after the finish and draws the new column ($2858 left, $23EE right, with $F1A5/$F16D, $E6EC/$E72F); then the screen shift ($1395), $E6BE, the effect sprites ($147A), $BCD3, $B34F, $38C4 and $B4A8 ($E6BE, $147A, $BCD3 and $B4A8 only outside a heavy pass, $1B3E; $38C4 only while $1B46 is 0; with $1B7F set 16 calls of the NOP slide replace $B4A8), and, while the scroll speed $208C is 0, the end of a lost life when $1B80 runs out ($3B3F with A = 0 after a pit fall with $1BBA set, else $BDC1 and $3B3F with A = $1BEC).

The opcode at $1FB2 switches the object updates: CLC ($18, written by $1D23 at the level start) makes the BCC that follows skip them; $B39A writes another opcode (SEC, by its effect) to let them run. Then $C18A, $C8A0, $ECF1 (happy land) and $B645 run one after another while the raster is outside the middle band ($1BA9 = 0). From $1FD5: unless paused, starts and plays the sound effects ($BC99) and the music ($087B); in the happy land counts $1B95 down and makes asked-for tune changes ($E4C5); then, outside a heavy pass and the middle band: $37E9 (before the finish), the $1B79 countdown ($361C), $3888/$3796 or $3757/$356D by $3507, $364E and $1B68; after the finish the stage ends when $1BC7 runs out ($3B3F with A = 1), otherwise $BE08. Clears $1B3E and loops.
Common head of every handler in the play-time raster chain: saves A, X and Y in zero page $0C-$0E and acknowledges the raster interrupt.
Sets the next link of the play-time raster chain: A is the raster line, X/Y the handler's address, written straight into the hardware vector $FFFE/$FFFF (the KERNAL is switched out in play).
Common tail of the play-time raster chain: restores A, X and Y from $0C-$0E and returns from the interrupt.

One frame of horizontal scroll. Subtracts the operand at $208C (the scroll speed) from the fine scroll in $10 and keeps its low three bits. When it passes a character, steps the coarse column $0F by $1B3F: scrolling left it counts down and wraps from 0 to 39; scrolling right it counts up to 40 and wraps from 40 to 0 (the test is CMP #$29 at $20C1), so it takes 41 values that way; each wrap sets $1BDD to $27 and increments $1B48. Sets $1B3C. Then, unless $1BC9 is set, sets the frame flag $1B3B.
Operand of SBC #$00 at $208B: the scroll speed in pixels a frame, written by the play loop ($1EF5), $1CCE, the pause ($2270, $2296) and others; the fine and coarse scroll steps follow.

Sets the background colour $D021. While the counter in the operand at $20E2 runs (counting down unless $1B68 is set), the colour comes from the table at $BE38 until an entry with bit 7 set; otherwise from the operand at $20F3.
Operand of LDX #$00 at $20E1: the background colour flash counter, written by $1C39 (0), $3B60 and $BE1E, counted down at $20EA unless $1B68 is set.
Operand of LDA #$FF at $20F2: the background colour when no flash runs, written from the land's $9093 at the level start ($1E2B) and zeroed by $1100 during the reveal.

The handler that ends the frame's raster chain: sets the next interrupt to $213D at line $2F, runs $C0DC, sets both character multicolours to the operands at $2108/$210D, sets the background colour ($20E1), then the border: colour from the operand at $211A when $1C19 is 0, otherwise $B293 when $1BC9 is negative, or else the panel ($E426) and, when $1BD1 is set, $B312. Always ends with $BDD7.
Operand of LDA #$FF at $2107: multicolour 1 for the playfield ($D022), written by $1CB5 from the land's $908F; then multicolour 2.
Operand of LDA #$FF at $210C: multicolour 2 ($D023), written by $1CBB from the land's $9091.
Operand of LDA #$FF at $2119: the border colour while $1C19 is 0; then the panel and status border routines.

First half of a double interrupt that lands the next one on an exact cycle. Saves A, Y and X in the operands of the loads at $21AE-$21B3 and the stack pointer in the operand at $21A7, sets the next interrupt for line $30 at $2162, re-enables interrupts and runs into the NOP slide at $B17A, where the second interrupt arrives with at most a cycle of jitter.

Second half: VSP, the trick that scrolls the playfield sideways without moving a character. Patches its own JSR at $2196 to enter the NOP slide at $B182 + coarse column/2 ($0F: 0-39, and 40 for a step when scrolling right, $20C1), sets the fine scroll from $10 with multicolour on, waits in the slide, then writes $12 and $1B to $D011 on line $30: the bad line starts late by that many cycles, and the video chip draws the whole screen shifted by as many characters. Sets the next handler ($21EE at line $52), restores the stack pointer and registers saved by $213D, and sets $D018 from the operand at $21AA.
Operand of LDA #$EE at $2177: low byte of the handler after the VSP interrupt, written by $1C3D; the VSP timing follows.
Operand of LDA #$21 at $217C: high byte of the handler after the VSP, written by $1C40.
Operand of LDX #$52 at $2181: the raster line of the handler after the VSP, written by $1C43.
Low byte of the JSR into the NOP slide at $2196, written by $216D from the coarse column ($0F/2 + $82): this sets the cycle of the VSP write.
High byte of the VSP slide JSR, written by $2174 ($B1).

Operand of LDY #$1B at $2199: the second value written to $D011 by the VSP write. $1B shows the playfield (written by $114C); $5B adds extended colour to multicolour, an invalid mode that shows black (written by $1CCA and the land's $A5C5).
Operand of LDX #$00 at $21A6: the stack pointer saved by $214C before the stabilising interrupt; $21A8 TXS restores it, dropping the interrupted frame of the NOP-slide wait.
Operand of LDA #$FF at $21A9: the $D018 value written each frame after the VSP: $1F (screen $4400) or $2F ($4800), set by $1C98 and flipped by $2667 to swap the screens.
Operand of LDA #$00 at $21AE: A saved by $213D.
Operand of LDX #$00 at $21B0: X saved by $2143.
Operand of LDY #$00 at $21B2: Y saved by $2140; the RTI follows.

An extra raster handler that $E2F0-$E341 splices into the play-time chain (it writes $B5/$21 through ($D4) into one band's next link, at line $62, $82, $A2 or $C2 from $F96F, and sets $1BB6 = 1): its own next link is the band it displaced (line and handler patched into $21B9/$21BB/$21BD from $F973-$F97E). When $1BB6 is set and $1B9C is not, it colours sprites 6 and 7 (the player) 6 and $0E unless $1BC2 and $E44B are both set, then shows effect sprite $1B73's frame ($1B6D,X) through sprite 5's pointer on both screens.
Operand of LDA #$72 at $21B8: the raster line of $21B5's next link, written by $E31E from $F973.
Operand of LDX #$10 at $21BA: low byte of $21B5's next handler, written by $E324 from $F977.
Operand of LDY #$22 at $21BC: high byte of $21B5's next handler, written by $E32A from $F97B.

Raster handler: next link $2210 at line $72. Stores X (1, left by $206B) in $1BA9 unless $1B7F is set, calls the band routine $C0xx whose low byte $29CA patches from the land's choice (as loaded $C0DB), and $BA08 while $1BC9 is 0.
Low byte of the JSR $C0xx in $21EE, written by $29CA from the land's choice at $90B0 (the table $29EC): which band routine this raster band runs.
Raster handler: next link $2222 at line $92; calls the band routine $C0xx whose low byte $29D4 patches (as loaded $C0DB).
Low byte of the JSR $C0xx in $2210, written by $29D4.

Raster handler: next link $229C at line $B2; calls the band routine $C0xx whose low byte $29DE patches (as loaded $C0DB). Then reads the pause key unless $1BD1 is set or $208C is 8. With the stick centred and RUN/STOP down ($DC01 bit 7) it pauses: $1BC5 = 1, $1BD7 kept in $1BD8 and $208C in the operand at $2295, both zeroed, and $0D1B silences the SID. While paused, RUN/STOP released with the stick moved resumes: $1BC5 = 0 and $1BD7 and $208C restored. Ends through the scroll step at $2088.
Low byte of the JSR $C0xx in $2222, written by $29DE; the pause key test follows.
Operand of LDA #$FF at $2294: the scroll speed kept while paused, written by $2264 from $208C; the resume path loads it back into $208C.
Raster handler: next link $22BA at line $D2; stores $00 (X from $206B, 1, less one) in $1BA9, calls the band routine $C0xx whose low byte $29E8 patches (as loaded $C0DB), and $F07E while $1B3E is 0.
Low byte of the JSR $C0xx in $229C, written by $29E8.

Raster handler: next link $18C1 at line $EE; calls $BAC3 and $349C, then sets the low byte of $18D3's JSR into the NOP slide from the table at $3483, indexed by sprite 7's Y position when it is between $DA and $F1 (0 otherwise).

Raster handler at line $FA: next link $20F8 at line 0. Unless the coarse column has just wrapped ($1B48) or the game is paused it runs $3A88; with $1C19 set and $1BC9 clear, $B62A unless $1B48 is set. Then, when $1BC3 is set, the playfield scrolls ($208C nonzero), the land asks for it ($9023) and $1C19 and $1BC9 are not both set, rotates two glyphs of the character set as one 16-pixel-wide strip (8 rows; $7FC8 and $7FD0 as loaded, the land picks them through $9024 and $BBC8-$BBE0) by $1BD7/2 bits a frame, or when that is 0 by one bit on the frames where $1B68 is 1, left or right against the scroll direction $1B3F, so their pattern drifts. When the rotation is skipped because $208C or $9023 is 0 or $1BC9 is set (not when $1BC3 is 0), it calls $EE11 if $903C and $1BEC are set. With $1C19 set: while $1BC9 is set (the walk-in at the level start) it re-raises the frame flag, moves the player's X ($1BE3) by $CF18 indexed by the step counter $1B81 (one step a frame down to $41, then two; on reaching $34 it clears $1B52, raises $1B54 and calls $33F4; when the count runs out it stays at 0 and $1B54 is cleared), and runs $EE9E and $147A itself; then, walk-in or not, in the happy land ($1BEC) with $903B set, looks at the map byte in front of the player (($8A) + $51/$52 by direction): glyphs $60-$61 while $1BB6 is 0 run $E2F0, glyphs $62-$63 while it is 1 run $E2D2.

Low byte of the LDA $7FD0,X at $2336 in the glyph rotation; $BBD7 rewrites the rotation's glyph addresses ($2337/$2338, $233E/$233F, $2350/$2351) from the land's glyph number $9024, so the land chooses which two glyphs drift.
High byte of the LDA $7FD0,X at $2336, written by $BBE0 with the rotated glyph's address.
Low byte of the ROR $7FC8,X at $233A (the first rotated glyph), written by $BBB9; $BBB9-$BBC8 write the first glyph's address into $233B/$233C, $234C/$234D and $2353/$2354.
High byte of the ROR $7FC8,X at $233A, written by $BBC2.
Low byte of the ROR $7FD0,X at $233D, written by $BBD1 together with $2337 and $2350 (the second glyph of the pair; the first, $7FC8, is in the operands at $233B, $234C, $2353).
High byte of the ROR $7FD0,X at $233D, written by $BBDA; then the loop end and the leftward rotation.
Low byte of the LDA $7FC8,X at $234B (leftward rotation, first glyph), written by $BBBF.
High byte of the LDA $7FC8,X at $234B, written by $BBC8.
Low byte of the ROL $7FD0,X at $234F, written by $BBD4.
High byte of the ROL $7FD0,X at $234F, written by $BBDD.
Low byte of the ROL $7FC8,X at $2352, written by $BBBC.
High byte of the ROL $7FC8,X at $2352, written by $BBC5.

Low byte of a tile's address for each value of a tile number's low nibble: $09 + 16*n. With the high nibble + $80 as the high byte ($2610-$2618), tile t's 16 glyph numbers sit at $8009 + 16*t (Y adds 0-15).

Advances the map by one character column at both screen edges (called each pass while $1B3C counts characters, from $1CE6 and $1F48): the right edge's column within the tile $1BCA steps 0-3; on passing a tile it advances the map column $1BD9, skipping marker columns (band 0 byte $F0 or more: $2A20 handles their tune change unless $1BC9 is set), handles repeat markers ($269F), runs $F121 and points the band pointers at the new column ($2631). The left edge ($1BCB, $1BDA, $26E4) follows the same way. Then works out where on the screens the new column goes ($39/$3E, $3B, from $1BDD, $1B40, $1B41, $1B44 and $0F); if the coarse column has wrapped ($1B48) it swaps the screens ($2667) and moves the colour RAM up a row and left a column (the VSP offset dropping by 40 + 1: columns 0-37 of rows 0-23 from columns 1-38 of rows 1-24, X = 0 to $25 in each loop); finally draws the new column ($27FF) and, after a wrap, recolours it ($2550).

Rewrites the colour RAM for one screen column from the glyphs of the screen to be shown ($29A5) through the land's colour table $8900: four groups of six rows ($3D = 3 to 0), 24 rows in all. Sets $1B3E = 3 so the play loop skips its game work for this pass. When $1B42 is set it steps the six LDY operands ($2568 and on) by one and goes round again, so a neighbouring column is coloured too; then clears $1B42.
Operand of LDY #$00 at $2567: the column offset in the recolour loop, stepped with the five LDY operands below it ($2572, $257C, $2586, $2590, $259A, rows 1-5) by $25AD-$25D1.
Operand of LDY #$28 at $2571 in the recolour loop: row 1's offset, stepped with $2568 by $25B0/$25C5; the rest of the recolour rows and the column step follow.
Operand of LDY #$50 at $257B in the recolour loop: row 2's offset, stepped with $2568 by $25B3/$25C8.
Operand of LDY #$78 at $2585: row 3's offset in the recolour loop, stepped by $25B6/$25CB.
Operand of LDY #$A0 at $258F: row 4's offset, stepped by $25B9/$25CE.
Operand of LDY #$C8 at $2599: row 5's offset, stepped by $25BC/$25D1; then the six-row step and the second-column pass.

Points the six band pointers $C6/$C7 ... $D0/$D1 at the tiles of map column Y: for each band k = 0-5 reads the tile number from the band's row of the map ($8A00 + $100*k, through the pointer table at $CF9B, patched into the LDA at $2603) and turns it into the tile's address ($23DE for the low byte, $80 + the high nibble for the high byte). Then sets $3D and $40 to the tile column in the operand at $2621 (0 from $2631, 3 from $264C, or $1BCA/$1BCB, 0-3, from $31F2/$3251), $3F = $D8 (colour RAM), and returns A = the shown screen's page ($29A5).
Operand of LDY #$74 at $25F5: the map column, stored by $25F0.
Operand of the LDA $8F00,Y at $2603: the band's map row, low byte, written from $CF9B.
High byte of the band's map row ($8A-$8F), written from $CF9C.
Operand of LDY #$00 at $2620: the tile column to start at, 0 for the right edge ($2633) and 3 for the left edge ($264E).
The tail of $25F0 without re-reading the map: sets $3D/$40 to Y, $3F = $D8, and returns the shown screen's page ($29A5).
Entry used by $F172 and $2622: returns the shown screen's page ($29A5 by $1B3A).
The right edge entered a new tile: tile column 0, band pointers for map column $1BD9 ($25F0), then $2642.
Sets the right edge's band pointers for map column $1BD9 starting at tile column Y (stored in $2621); called also by $31F2 when the direction reverses.
The right edge stays in its tile: $2622 with Y = $1BCA, then $2642.
Common end of the right-edge set-up: $3A = the shown screen's page, $3C = the hidden one; $1BCA = Y.
The left edge's counterpart of $2631: tile column 3, map column $1BDA.
Sets the left edge's band pointers for map column $1BDA from tile column Y; called also by $3251.
The left edge stays in its tile: $2622 with Y = $1BCB; the pages go the other way round ($3C shown, $3A hidden) and Y is stored in $1BCB.
Swaps the shown and hidden screens: flips the $D018 value at $21AA ($1F/$2F, screen $4400/$4800) and $1B3A.
Clears $1B41, $1B43, $1B44 and $1B45 (X = 0). $267A is the same with X given.
Clears $1B41, $1B43, $1B44 and $1B45 with the value in X (called with X = 0 by $2981).
The new screen column being drawn, 24 glyph numbers in six groups of four (one group per map band): rows 0-3, filled by $27FF from band 0's tile.
Rows 4-7 of the new column (band 1's tile).
Rows 8-11 (band 2).
Rows 12-15 (band 3).
Rows 16-19 (band 4).
Rows 20-23 (band 5).

A map column code in A from band 0, at the right edge: codes below $D0 are ordinary tiles. $D0-$DF and $E0-$EF are repeat markers: the land's table at $9000 (pair n = code AND $0F) gives a count ($50) and a length ($51), and the edge's map column $1BD9 jumps back by the length until the count ($1BDB) runs out, so a stretch of map is drawn several times. $1B49 records which edge started the current repeat. Uses $27CC-$27F0.
The left edge's handling of repeat markers (map column $1BDA, counter $1BDC), the mirror of $269F, so both edges agree on where a repeat starts and ends.
Repeat markers met by the left edge while scrolling the other way ($2880): steps $1BDA forward by the length while the count $1BDC lasts.
Repeat markers met by the right edge while scrolling the other way ($289E), counter $1BDB.
Ends a repeat: the edge's counter ($1BDB,X) = $FF and $1B49 = 0.
$1BD9,X + 1 (X = 0 right edge, 1 left edge).
$1BD9,X + the repeat length $51.
$1BD9,X - the repeat length $51.
A $D0-$DF marker starts a repeat: the edge's counter = 0 and $1B49 = 1.
An $E0-$EF marker starts a repeat: counter 0, $1B49 = $FF.
A = $1BDC - 1.
A = $1BDB - 1.
Repeat marker A: count to $50 and length to $51 from the land's pair table at $9000 + 2*(A AND $0F).

Draws the new screen column: gathers its 24 glyphs from the six band tiles at the current tile column ($40 + $0C, then up a row of the tile at a time) into $2687-$269E, then writes them down the column on both screens ((39) and (3B)) and their colours from the land's table $8900 into colour RAM ((3E)), 24 rows.

Moves the map one character column the other way (called from the play loop at $1F37 when the scroll direction $1B3F is 1): the left edge's tile column $1BCB counts down, on leaving a tile $1BDA goes back past marker columns (a band-0 code of $F0 or more twelve columns on runs $2A1B), repeat markers ($2724) and the band pointers ($264C); the right edge likewise ($1BCA, $1BD9, $2767, $F13E). Then the screen addresses, and on a coarse wrap ($1B48) the screen swap and the colour RAM moved down a row in the same columns (+40: rows 0-13 into 1-14 for columns 0-38, rows 15-23 into 16-24 for columns 1-38; row 14 goes to row 15 through $BFCF, columns 1-38 only: column 0 of row 14 is saved and not put back), the shift state cleared, the column drawn ($27FF) and recoloured ($2550 with Y = 0, rows 0-23, then column 0 of row 24, where its pointers end).
The page of the screen shown (from the next frame) for each value of $1B3A: entry 0 $48, entry 1 $44; read by $255A and $262D, and by $13DB, which flips it (EOR $0C) to reach the hidden screen.

Raster band set chosen by a map object code A ($78-$7F), called by $E704 when the code is met moving left (from $E6EC, the play loop's path for $1B3F = 1): X = A - $79, then $29B0. Moving right, $E777 enters at $29AC instead, X = A - $78, so moving left picks the set one lower, the one before the marker.
Entry used by $E777 (moving right, $1B3F = 0): X = A - $78, then $29AF. (Entered from $29A7 only when A - $79 borrowed.)

Applies band routine set X (unless it is the one in $1BCE already): four entries from the land's table at $90B0 + 4*X, each an index into $29EC, give the low bytes of the JSR $C0xx in the four raster bands ($2203, $221D, $222F, $22AD). Called at the level start ($1D8D) with the land's $9706.
Low bytes of the three band routines a land can choose: $C0DB, $C01C, $C07C.

Colour set chosen by a map object code A ($70-$77; called by $E70F when it is met moving left: X = A - $71; $29F4, called by $E782 moving right, gives X = A - $70): unless set X is already in $1BCF, copies three bytes from the land's $9095 + 3*X into $1B8B-$1B8D.
Entry used by $E782 (moving right): X = A - $70, the colour set choice one above the leftward one.

A tune marker column (band 0 code $F0 or more) met by the left edge while scrolling back ($2873): X = code - $F1 (code $F0 gives $0F), one less than $2A20 gives, so passing a marker backwards picks the tune before it. When X differs from $1BD0, records it and, in the happy land ($1BEC), asks for tune X ($1B97 = X, $1B98 = 1).
A tune marker column met by the right edge ($240A): X = code - $F0, then as $2A1B.

Works out where the player is in the map from the Y position $1BE4 less the slope offset $1B4B. At $DA or more (below the map) it only counts $1B7D (fallen out) and leaves $1B4C at 1. Otherwise it clears $1B4C, takes the character row ($1BE4 - $32)/8 into $1BE6, the screen column into $1BE5 ($12 moving right, $11 moving left, plus the coarse column $0F; in a pass where the coarse column has just wrapped, $1B48, plus $27 when $0F is 0 or 0 otherwise, or $29 and $FF when on a slope, $1B74), and points $8A/$8B at that row and column of the shown screen ($1AEA/$1B03, plus $3481 for the screen). The tests that follow read the glyphs around the player at ($8A) + 0-3 (head), +$28/$50 (body) and +$78-$7A (under the feet).
Operand of ADC #$12 at $2A8D: the player's column on the screen, $12 moving right or $11 moving left, written by $2A89.

Glyph threshold for the floor tests ($2D43, $2D69, $2DC7, $2E39, ...): glyphs below it are solid. $2AAF stores the land's $9020 (walls and platforms: $39 in Jellyland) while the player walks or falls, and $9021 (walls only: $2F) while he rises or drops through a platform, so he jumps up through platforms and lands on them. Also written by $2ED0.

The player's movement for one pass (from the play loop, $1ED5, while $1BD1 and $1B7F are 0); once the player has fallen out ($1B7E) it goes straight to $315A. Picks the solid threshold ($2AAE) and sets the in-air flag $1B5B: 0 while the drop-through timer $1B61 runs (counted down here), else $1B59 when rising or $1B5A (falling). A pending knock-back ($1B9F = 1, written by $C715) first stops the run ($2C3E, $2B6E) while the scroll moves, then becomes a jump of strength $12 ($2EB5) against the direction of travel ($1BA0 = $FF moving right, 1 moving left; $1B9F = $FF meanwhile). Otherwise, unless $1BC6 is set, the walk and jump logic ($2B7F) and, with the land's $903C, the skid glyph test $EE74. Then $315A; a check of the glyph at the player's middle ($8A + $29) against the land's $9025-$9028 sets $1B4F ($E0 for $9025/$9026, 0 for $9027/$9028); $E253; and, in the happy land with $CF8B set and $1BC6 clear, a glyph $16-$17 under the player's feet ($8A + $79) ends the stage: $1BC6 is set, sounds $1E and $1F play and $BB69 runs.
Offsets $51 and $52 into the map rows from ($8A), by the scroll direction $1B3F: the glyph in front of the player, read by $23B8.
Slopes: unless $1B74 is negative, $2EF9 updates the slope state, and $3012 runs when $1B74 is then 0 (not on a slope); with $1B74 negative $3012 runs at once.

Walking against walls: sets $1B4C, works out the map pointer ($2A3A) unless the player has fallen out ($1B7D), updates slopes ($2B6E) and the vertical movement ($2CAB). Then, by the scroll speed and the stick (left $1BE0, right $1BE1, 0 = pressed) or the scroll direction, tests the three rows beside the player on the side he moves to (($8A) + 0/$28/$50, only the lower two, + $28/$50, when ducking or in the air; columns 0 or 3): a wall glyph (below the land's $9021) calls $2C26; when nothing blocks, the facing request $1B5E becomes $FF (left), 1 (right) or 0, or keeps the bounce direction $1BA0.
The player meets a wall: at full speed ($1B51 = $5D), not on a slope ($1B74 = 0) and with no dust puff running ($1B55 = 0), $F043 runs with A = 3 (a bump); in every case it then goes on into $2C3E.

Stops the player's run: unless he is on a slope outside a bounce (then returns A = $1B74), clears the speed $1B51 and the facing request $1B5E, lets the scroll finish its character ($1BD7 = 1, with $1B4E evened down, unless the fine scroll $10 is already at the edge, 0 or 7 by direction, when $1BD7 = 0), plays sound 6 and runs $33C9 when $1B52 was not 0, and clears $1BCC, $1B54 and $1B47; a finished bounce ($1B9F and $1BA0 both set) is cleared. Returns A = 0.
Frames the player drops through a platform after down and fire, by $1BB6: 8 or $10 ($2D1D into $1B61).

Jumping, falling and ducking. $1B5F stays 1 while up has been held since the last jump in the air, so a new jump needs up released. Rising ($1B59) goes to $2D85, falling ($1B5A) to $2E1A. On the ground: up starts a jump (from a slope the slope offset is folded into the Y position first, doubled when $1BB6 is set) through $2D62; down sets the duck flag $1B62, and down with fire (above line $BD) the drop-through timer $1B61. With no floor under the feet (both glyphs at $8A + $79/$7A at or above the threshold) he starts falling ($1B5A = 1, $1B5D = 0); with a floor his Y snaps to the row ($2D56).
Puts the player's Y on his character row: $1BE4 = $CB7A + $1BE6 ($35 + 8 per row); then clears a finished bounce ($2C96).

Starts a jump if there is headroom: with a solid glyph above the head ($8A + 1/2) it snaps to the row and plays sound $0D instead; otherwise sets the rising flag $1B59, the jump index $1B5D = $17, and plays the jump sound ($BFCD by $1BB6).

One frame of rising: releasing up early ($1BDE not 0) cuts the jump index $1B5D down to 6 (variable jump height; $1B60 marks it, $1B94 skips the test). When the index runs out the player starts falling ($1B5A = 1). Otherwise a solid glyph above the head ($2DF5) stops the jump: falling starts and, unless $1B52 is set, $1BBB = 10 and $1BE4 drops by 3. Else the index counts down (with $1BB6 set only while $1B68 and $1B66 are both nonzero, a floatier jump) and Y rises by the speed $33B3 gives for the index, but not above line $34.

One frame of falling: the index $1B5D counts up to $1F and Y grows by the speed $33A1 gives. With a solid glyph under a foot ($8A + $79, else $7A) and the three rows above that glyph clear, the player lands; moving left, a solid glyph in the next column as well ($8A + $7A or $7B) lands him without the test of the rows above: after a long fall ($1B5D $1B or more) $F043 runs with A = 2, falling and in-air flags clear, Y snaps to the row and sound $0D plays. Below the map ($1B4C set) a Y of $F4 or more (less the slope offset) is a fall into a pit: $1B7E counts it, and $1B80 = $28 frames before the play loop ends the life ($1BBA is raised too when, in a sad land with $36F3 set, glyph $4C or $4E is found at $8A + $50-$52).

Starts a forced jump of strength A ($1B5D) with X kept in the operand at $2ED7: rising and in-air flags set, falling and slope offset cleared, the threshold set to walls only ($9021), then one frame of rising ($2D85). Returns X. Called by $2AE7 (A = $12, the knock-back), $311C (A = 6, off the top of a slope), $B59A (A = $0D) and $C6FE (A = $20).
Operand of LDX #$FF at $2ED6: the X saved by $2EB5.
Slope offsets in pixels for fine scroll 0-7: 4 4 3 3 2 2 1 1 (slope glyph 0, $9081; moving right, $2F35-$2F3A also use it for slope glyph 2, $9083).
Slope offsets for fine scroll 0-7: 8 8 7 7 6 6 5 5 (slope glyphs 1 and 3, $9082 and $9084).
Slope offsets, all 0: slope glyph 2 ($9083) when the slope is met moving left ($2FAD); moving right, $2F35 uses $2ED9 for that glyph instead.
High bytes of the slope offset table for slope glyphs 0-3 (all $2E).
Low bytes of the slope offset tables: $D9, $E1, $E9, $E1.

On a slope: while the player moves (falling, or the scroll speed $208C not 0), looks at the glyphs beside his feet (($8A) + $52/$53, $78-$7C, by direction) for the land's slope glyphs $9081-$9084, steps him a row up ($311F) or down ($3137) where the land's $9085-$9087 mark a slope's end, and sets the slope offset $1B4B from the table of the slope glyph that matched (one of four, $2EF1/$2EF5), indexed by the fine scroll $10 (the LDA at $2F4A/$2FBB is patched with the table's address). $1B74 = 1 while a slope glyph is found, 0 otherwise (clearing $1B4B).
Low byte of LDA $FFFF,X at $2F4A: the slope table, patched by $2F45 from $2EF5.
High byte of that LDA, patched by $2F3F from $2EF1.
Low byte of LDA $FFFF,X at $2FBB, patched by $2FB6.
High byte, patched by $2FB0.

Slope heights in pixels for fine scroll 0-7, 1 1 2 2 3 3 4 4 ($2FF2-$2FF9): the table of the first slope character $9088, read by $3012 through the LDA $FFFF,X at $3063/$30D4, whose operand $300A/$300E point here. $2FFA (5) begins the next table.

Bytes 1-5 of the slope height table $2FFA (5 5 6 6 7 7 8 8 for fine scroll 0-7, $2FFA-$3001; slope characters $9089 and $908B), read through $3063/$30D4. The same bytes from $2FFB (5 6 6 7 7, then 8 8 at $3000) are also read by $C79C as $2FFB+Y, Y being the operand of the LDY at $C79A, and written into $1325 before sound 3 plays: the pitch steps up as Y grows.

The end of the slope height table $2FFA (8, 8), then $3002-$3009, eight zeros: the height table of slope character $908A when $3012 meets it in direction 0 ($30C6). $C79C's table for sound 3's effect ($2FFB+Y into $1325) runs into these bytes for Y of 5 or more; the range of Y is not established.

High bytes ($2F, $2F, $30, $2F) of the four slope height tables, one per slope character $9088-$908B matched by $3012: $3058 and $30C9 store them into the high byte of the LDA $FFFF,X at $3063/$30D4 ($3065, $30D6). With the low bytes at $300E the tables are $2FF2, $2FFA, $3002 and $2FFA, indexed by the fine scroll ($10).
Low bytes ($F2, $FA, $02, $FA) of the four slope height tables whose high bytes are at $300A; $305E and $30CF store them into $3064 and $30D5.

Works out the height adjustment $1B4B for the ground under the player, from the characters around the player's screen position ($8A/$8B) and the land's character codes at $9088-$908E. Returns at once when $1B5A and the scroll speed ($208C) are both 0. With $1B74 = 0 it only tests whether the player stands on one of the four slope characters $9088-$908B ($30DB: $1B74 = $FF if so, 0 if not). With $1B74 set, it follows the slope: in direction $1B3F = 1 it steps the position up a row ($311F) while the character at offset $50 is $908C, goes to $310B on $908D, and otherwise looks the character up in $9088-$908B (taking $908A as $9088) and loads $1B4B from that slope's height table ($2FF2, $2FFA or $3002, addressed through $300A/$300E) at the fine scroll ($10); in direction 0 it reads offsets $76, $79, $4F and $7A and steps down a row ($3137) instead. Called from $2B7B.
Operand (low byte) of the LDA $FFFF,X at $3063, the slope's height table, set from $300E by $305E.
Operand (high byte) of the LDA at $3063, set from $300A by $3058.
Operand (low byte) of the LDA $FFFF,X at $30D4, the slope's height table, set from $300E by $30CF.
Operand (high byte) of the LDA at $30D4, set from $300A by $30C9.
The player has run off the top of a slope (character $908D): steps the position up a row ($311F), clears $1B74 and $1B4B ($3102), and when $1B51 is $50 or more calls $2EB5 with A = 6.
Moves the player's screen position one character row up: $1BE4 (the player's Y in pixels) less 8, the row counter $1BE6 less 1, and the screen pointer $8A/$8B less 40.
Moves the player's screen position one character row down: $1BE4 plus 8, $1BE6 plus 1, the screen pointer $8A/$8B plus 40.
Clears the duck flag $1B62 and jumps to $EF86 with X = the scroll direction $1B3F.

The player's horizontal movement for one pass, from the decoded stick and the facing $1B5E. While $1B46 or $1B47 counts, or $1B7E is set, it only keeps the speed going ($32DE, $326C). Down ($1B62) sets $1B63; when nothing solid is at the top row of the player's position (the glyphs at offsets 0-3 of $8A all $9021 or higher), it also sets, with speed ($208C), $1B54 and runs $3388. When the facing differs from the scroll direction $1B3F it turns round: at the edge of a character (fine scroll 7 going right, 0 going left) it calls $E668/$E630 and $2633/$264E, moves the column wrap counter $1BDD, sets $1B41 and $1B3F to the new direction, and starts the six-pass turn counter $1B46. Otherwise it accelerates or brakes through the speed counter $1B51 (0 to $5D), the charge flags $1B52-$1B54 and the fire bit ($1BE2, when $1BEB allows it), and ends with the scroll speed in $1BD7 from the speed table ($3392). Called from $2B1B.
Operand of the LDX #$FF at $31F5: X (0) kept across the turn-round calls by $31E9.
Operand of the LDX #$FF at $3254: X (1) kept across the turn-round calls by $3248.
Operand of the LDA #$FF at $335A: the charge flag $1B54 as it was before $32FF cleared it, stored by $32FC.
Copies the charge flag $1B52 into $1B54 when $1B54 is clear; if that made it set, falls into $3388.
Unless $1B58 is set, calls $33F4 with A = 0 (effect sprite and sound).
Returns in X the scroll speed for the speed counter Y ($1B51): the byte at $CF19+Y, halved (at least 1) when $1BB6 is set.
A plus the step from the table $3460 at X (halved when $1BB6 is set; the step is patched into the ADC at $33B0). Called from $2E28.
Operand of the ADC at $33B0: the step $33A1 adds, from $3460 (halved when $1BB6 is set).
A less the step from the table $3460 at X (halved when $1BB6 is set) and less the slope height $1B4B. Called from $2DE4.
Operand of the SBC at $33C2: the step $33B3 subtracts, from $3460 (halved when $1BB6 is set).
Stores A (0 from the callers seen) into $1B4E, $1B50, $1B52 and $1B53; when $1B56 is 0 also clears $1B55 and $1B58. If $1B9C is clear and $1B55 was set, falls into $33EB.
Sets both frames of the effect sprite (sprite 4, alternated by $B293 from $1B6D/$1B6E) to block $0F, the blank sprite.

Saves A; unless the $1B9C state runs, starts the effect sprite (sprite 4, drawn by $B293 from $1B69-$1B6E): $1B71 from $1474+$1BB6, $1B6B/$1B6C cleared ($BB9D, result 0 into $1B72), both frames blank ($33EB), $1B73 = 1. Then, when the saved A is 0 and $1B5B is clear, falls into $341E (sound $BFCB). Called from $2397, $3360, $338F, $BB76, $E2FF and others.
Operand of the LDX #$FF at $3406: X kept across $33F4 (stored at $33FA).
Plays sound effect number $BFCB+$1BB6 through $134F, keeping X (patched into the LDX at $342B).
Operand of the LDX #$FF at $342B: X kept across $341E (stored at $341E).
32 bytes, 1 rising to 3 (twenty-four 1s, five 2s, three 3s); read at $B592 indexed by a counter.

The vertical steps of the player's death leap ($BD5A), read as $344E + $1BC8: -4 ($FC) rising to 0; the index runs on into $3460 (steps up to 8) and stops at the first 8, so he rises, slows and falls ever faster.
Movement steps 0,1,0,1,1,2,1,2... up to 8, read by $33A1 and $33B3 indexed by X.
Two bytes, $04 and $00, read at $2AA8.

25 low bytes of entry points into the NOP slide at $B100+ ($7B-$84): $22E0 picks one by sprite 7's Y position (when it is $DA-$F1) and patches it into the JSR at $18D3, presumably to make up for the cycles the player's sprites take on the panel's lines.

Sets up sprites 0-5 for the score panel on line $E5: X positions from $EFB8, pointers from $EFBE written to both screens' sprite pointer tables ($47F8 and $4BF8), colours from $EFC4; enables all eight sprites, X high bit for sprite 5, X expansion of sprites 3 and 4 (keeping 6 and 7), no Y expansion, multicolour only for sprite 7, priority over the background for sprites 0-5. Called from the raster handler $22BA ($22C9) and from $F409.
The 16 score events' amounts, added by $350B to the digit $34F7 names: 1, 5, 2, 1, 5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 1, 2, 5, 8, 1, 1.

The 16 score events' digit positions in the score $CF78-$CF80 (0 is the most significant of nine): 8, 6, 6, 6, 7, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 2. With $34E7 the events are worth 1, 500, 200, 100, 50, 1000-5000, 10000, 20000, 50000, 80000, 100000 and 1000000 points.
Nonzero when the score has changed since it was last drawn: $350B stores the digit position in it, $356D clears it and redraws.
Adds score event number $F50D+X (Y) to the score; falls into $350B. Called from $C828.

Adds score event Y to the nine-digit decimal score $CF78-$CF80: amount $34E7+Y at digit $34F7+Y, carrying upward. Before the first change since the last redraw ($1B7A clear) it copies the score to $CF8C-$CF94 for $3578 to compare. Repeats $1B78 times (the bonus multiplier, when set). An extra life ($3636) comes from adding at the millions digit ($3530) or from the carry loop rolling the hundred-thousands digit over from 9 ($355A); a 100,000-point event (14) that itself takes that digit from 9 to 0 carries into the millions at $354B without reaching either test, so that million gives no life. Sets $3507 so the play loop redraws.
Operand of the LDX #$FF at $3566: how many more times $350B adds the event, the multiplier $1B78 less one (stored at $3527).
Operand of the LDX #$FF at $356A: X kept across $350B (stored at $350B).
When $3507 is set, clears it and redraws the score ($3578). Called from the play loop at $204E.
Redraws each score digit $CF78-$CF80 that differs from its copy at $CF8C-$CF94, through $389F into the score sprites (offsets $2D-$2F, $6D-$6F, $AD-$AF of page $40: sprites 0-2), then clears $1B7A.

Item effect 1 (the jump table at $F994/$F99D, entered from $BC52): raises the bonus multiplier $1B78 to 2 from none, otherwise by one, to at most 5; restarts its timer $1B79 = $C8, sets $1BBC/$1BBD = $1E and draws it ($360C).
Stores Y in the multiplier $1B78, draws digit Y at offset $8D of page $41 (a panel sprite, $38A1) and sets that sprite's colour $EFC0 to 6.

Lowers the bonus multiplier $1B78 by one: while it stays 2 or more, restarts its $C8-pass timer $1B79 and redraws it; at 1 or less clears it and sets the sprite colour $EFC0 to $0F. Called from the play loop at $202D when the timer $1B79 runs out.
One more life: plays sound $0F ($1352), adds a life ($3866), keeps X and Y (patched into the loads at $3644/$3646), and sets $1BC1 = $1E.
Operand of the LDY #$FF at $3644: Y kept across $3636.
Operand of the LDX #$FF at $3646: X kept across $3636.
Stores $1E in $1BC1. Jumped to from $10D8 and $BB8F.
Nonzero when the MAGIC counter $CF83-$CF85 has changed since it was drawn; set by $364F and $370F, cleared by $3757.

Adds one to the three-digit counter $CF83-$CF85, unless $1B64 is set. When $E5BE already equals the land's $9050, or the counter already equals the land's $9041-$9043 ($10ED), it plays sound $16 and adds nothing; otherwise it counts $E5BE up, plays sound $15 and adds. Before the first change since the last redraw ($1B7B clear) copies the counter ($36C3). In the happy land ($1BEC) with $CF8B set, reaching the land's $904D-$904F clears $CF8B and sets $18E4 = 1. Jumped to from $B581.
Copies the counter $CF83-$CF85 to $CF95-$CF97 for $3762 to compare, and sets $1B7B.

Item effect 2 (the jump table at $F994/$F99D): sets $1BBF = $1E and takes ten off the counter $CF83-$CF85 (a counter under 10 is first raised to 10, so it stops at 000) through $36EF with the tens digit, unless the quota flag $36F3 is already set; the raise to 10 happens before that test, so with $36F3 set a counter under 10 is left at 010, and $364E is not set for a redraw.

Takes one off the counter $CF83-$CF85 (the digit is patched into $3710) unless the quota-met flag $36F3 is set (the LDA #$FF at $36F2; written by $B7AE and $E566). When the counter reaches 000 it sets $36F3. Called from $3913 when a star is collected, and entry 5 of the item-effect table $F994/$F99D.

Operand of the LDA #$FF at $36F2, the star-quota flag: 0 while stars still count down the counter, nonzero once it has reached 000 ($3703). Cleared by $B7AE when the land changes state and set by $E566; read by $2E90, $3AC4, $BC34 and $F0D9.
Not referenced by any absolute address found: copies the counter for the redraw ($36C3) when $1B7B is clear, then falls into $370F to take one off it.

Takes one off the three-digit counter $CF83-$CF85 at the digit given by the operand of its LDX ($3710, written by $36EF: 2 for one, 1 for ten), borrowing, and sets $364E. In the happy land with $CF8B clear, when the counter is at or below the land's $904A-$904C it sets $CF8B. Called from $36F6 and $BEFC.
Operand of the LDX #$02 at $370F: the digit of $CF83-$CF85 that $370F takes one from, 2 (units) normally, 1 (tens) from $36D2.
When $364E is set, clears it and redraws the counter ($3762). Called from the play loop at $2048.
Redraws each digit of $CF83-$CF85 that differs from $CF95-$CF97, at offsets $2D-$2F of page $41 (a panel sprite), and clears $1B7B.
Nonzero when the time $CF86-$CF88 has changed since it was drawn; set by $37F8, cleared by $3796.
When $3795 is set, clears it and redraws the time ($37A1). Called from the play loop at $203D.
Redraws each digit of the time $CF86-$CF88 that differs from $CF98-$CF9A, at offsets $6D-$6F of page $41, and clears $1B7C.
Copies the time $CF86-$CF88 to $CF98-$CF9A for $37A1 to compare, and sets $1B7C.
The time 0 6 0, at which $37F8 sets $1BB8 and plays sound $17.
The time 0 3 0, the second point at which $37F8 sets $1BB8 and plays sound $17.
The clock: unless $1BB9 (time up) is set, counts $1BEA down and every $4B passes falls into $37F8. Called from the play loop at $201B.

Takes one off the three-digit time $CF86-$CF88, unless $1BAA is counting (then only $1BAA goes down: the wiki's extra-time POKE at $37FD). At 000 sets $1BB9 and jumps to $B5E9 (time up). At 060 and 030 increments $1BB8 and plays sound $17. Sets $3795 for the redraw.
Adds one to the two-digit lives counter $CF81-$CF82 and sets $3887 for the redraw; then falls into $387D.
Clears $1BB7 (the touch counter the wiki's invincibility POKE at $B61D hits) and sets $18EE = 1. Jumped to from $10D5 and $BB92.
Nonzero when the lives counter has changed since it was drawn; set by $3866 and at $BDC3, cleared by $3888.
When $3887 is set, clears it and draws the lives ($3892). Called from the play loop at $203A.
Draws the two lives digits $CF81 and $CF82 at offsets $EE and $EF of page $40 (sprite 3).
Draws digit Y (0-9) into sprite memory page $40 at offset X ($38A1 with A = $40).

Draws digit Y (0-9) into the panel's sprites: copies the digit's six bytes, from the address at $E372+Y (low) and $E382+Y (high), to page A at offset X and the five sprite rows below it (X+3 to X+15, every third byte). X and A are patched into the STA at $38BA.
Operand (low byte) of the LDA $FFFF,X at $38B7: the digit's glyph, from $E372+digit.
Operand (high byte) of the LDA at $38B7, from $E382+digit.
Operand (low byte) of the STA $FFFF,Y at $38BA: where in sprite memory the digit goes (X on entry to $38A1).
Operand (high byte) of the STA at $38BA: the sprite memory page, $40 or $41 (A on entry to $38A1).

In the happy land only ($1BEC): looks at four cells at the player, offsets $2A, $52, $29 and $51 from the screen position $8A (two columns, two rows), for a star, characters $FB-$FE. On a hit: keeps the offset in $EE0F, removes the star from both screens ($390B), from the map ($39A2), sets $0DFE to $A5 (or $05 when $CF8B is set) and scores event $EE10 ($350B) unless it is 5. Carry clear when nothing was found. Called from $1F6C. Its first opcode is rewritten by $B7CF from $B7D5+$1BEC: $A0 (LDY, the routine runs) in the happy land, $60 (RTS) in the sad one.

Removes a collected star: sound 7, one off the star counter ($36ED), then works out from the character it hit ($FB-$FE, a quarter of the 2x2 star, $3A82) where the star's top-left is, and writes the blank character $FF over its four cells in this screen ($8A) and the same cells in the other screen ($7E/$7F: the high byte EOR $0C swaps $44xx and $48xx) where they still hold star characters ($3A63). Leaves the star's top-left offset in $EE0F.
Operand of the ADC #$29 at $3941: the offset from the player's screen position to the star's cell in the other screen when it lies ahead ($27-$2A, set by $393B).
Operand of the SBC #$29 at $3954: the same offset when the star lies behind ($28-$2A, set by $394E).
Operand of the LDY #$FF at $3963: the star character that was hit ($FB-$FE), kept by $390B for $3A82.

Takes the collected star out of the level map: from the screen offset $8A + $EE0F picks the map page, $8A00-$8F00, one page for each band of four character rows (offsets $000-$09F, $0A0-$13F, $140-$1DF, $1E0-$27F, $280-$31F, $320-$3BF), finds the map byte at the player's column ($3A29) and, when it is one of the land's three star blocks $9037-$9039, decrements it (the block without the star).

Returns in X the index of the map byte for the player's column: starts at $1BDA and steps past five column entries (four when moving left, $1B3F = 1, with $1BCB clear), skipping bytes $D0 and above (which are not column entries), then any further $D0+ bytes.
Compares A with the land's three star block numbers $9037, $9038 and $9039; Z set on a match.
Writes the blank character $FF into two neighbouring cells (Y, Y+1) of the screen at $8A, and into the same cells of the other screen at $7E where they hold $FB or more. Returns A = Y+1.
X = Y - $FB: which quarter of the 2x2 star (0-3) the character Y is.

Animates characters in the land's character set each pass. In the happy land: when $1BD9 lies from the operand at $3A91 up to below the one at $3A95 (written by $E555/$E55B; $EE and $F9 in play) it rotates the bytes of characters $16-$17 ($78B0-$78BF) one step, when $1B68 and $CF8B are set; otherwise it runs the star animation ($3AEE). In the sad land: once the quota flag $36F3 and $1B68 are set, rotates characters $4C-$4D ($7A60-$7A6F) one step. Called from $22FF.
Operand of the CMP #$FF at $3A90, written by $E555: with the one at $3A95 it decides whether $1BD9 lets $3A88 skip the star animation; with both $FF it never does.
Operand of the CMP #$FF at $3A94, written by $E55B; see $3A91.

Every $EE10+1 passes ($1B75 counts) shows the next of 20 frames of the spinning star ($1B76 counts down): copies 32 bytes from the frame's address (low bytes $B47E, high $B492) to characters $FB-$FE, $7FD8-$7FF7. Only in the happy land: $3A88 comes here from its happy branch, $3AF3 tests $1BEC again, and $B7C9 writes this instruction's opcode from $B7D3 ($CE, DEC, when happy; $60, RTS, when sad). After each full turn the speed steps on: $1B77 counts down 26 entries of $EDF5 into $EE10, which is also the score event a star collected now gives ($38C4).
Operand (low byte) of the LDA $FFFF,X at $3B28: the star frame being copied, from $B47E.
Operand (high byte) of the LDA at $3B28, from $B492.
Jumps to $E2D2 when $1BB6 is set.
High bytes of the stage card's tune for $080C, by the sad/happy flag $1BEC: $FC (the tune at $FC56) and $FD ($FDB6).
Low bytes of the stage card's tune: $56 (sad) and $B6 (happy).

Starts or restarts a stage, and is where every way out of play leads ($1EBC quit, $1FA1, $1FAA, $205D, $CE52). Resets the stack, takes A as the new sad/happy flag $1BEC (0 sad, 1 happy; the old one kept in $3D9E), blanks the screen and both screens' characters, exchanges $7800-$7FFF with $D800-$DFFF ($3F52, swap 0), keeps $1BC6 and $1BBA in the operands at $3BB5/$3BBC and $1B78/$1BB8 in $F322/$F386, and calls $1BF3. Unless $1BC6 is set it resets the time from the land's table ($BD37) and the panel copies $CF8C-$CF9A and redraws the panel ($E589). Lives at $FF (game over, or Q in the pause) go to the game-over screen $3DEC; $1BC6 set goes to $F302; $1BBA set exchanges $D100-$D6FF with $6000-$65FF (swap 7), bringing in code the engine keeps under the I/O chips, calls $F451 and jumps to $638D in that code, which comes back through $3BCC to restart the stage happy. Otherwise it shows the stage card ($3BD6).
Operand of the LDA #$FF at $3BB4: $1BC6 as it was when the stage was (re)started ($3B7D); nonzero goes to $F302.
Operand of the LDA #$FF at $3BBB: $1BBA as it was when the stage was (re)started ($3B83); nonzero goes to the land's $638D.

The way back from the scene that $3BBF starts: reached by JMP $3BCC from code kept at $D5F5 (which swap 7 moves to $64F5): swaps $D100-$D6FF and $6000-$65FF back ($3F54 with X = 7) and restarts the stage with A = 1, the happy land ($3B3F).

The stage card before play. Fills the sprite block $43C0 with $AA, prints string 0 at $44D1, string 1 at $4428 and string 2 + $1BEC ("STATUS : SAD" or "STATUS : HAPPY!") at $474F through $B817; stores $E3F2+$1BEC in the land's $9122 and $E3F4+$1BEC in $9112; fills two bands of the screen with character $EE, draws the land's name strip from $BC59-$BC98 and $02A7-$02D6 with the colours $90ED-$90F6 and $9107 from the land's block; starts the sad or happy tune ($080C with $3B3B/$3B3D), sets up the sprites ($1A56, entry 1), X and Y expansion from the land's $9109/$910A. Each frame it runs $087B and the colour cycles ($B43D 2-5, $BE0D) and recolours the card's rows from $E3F6/$E406 (and $1000/$1008 when happy); after $BB37 ($50 frames, counted elsewhere) fire starts the stage: screen off, $ED98, $3F52, $B785 with A = $FF and on to play at $1D2F.
Operand of the LDA #$FF at $3D9D: the sad/happy flag from before $3B3F, passed to $B785, which swaps the land's sad and happy data when it differs from the new one.

Raster handler of the stage card's chain (installed through $F20F): calls $19DD, $ED65 and $BDD7, shows screen $4400, moves the five sprite X positions $910D-$9111 two pixels left (wrapping below $48 to $F8; the recorded stage card writes them to $D004-$D00C), sets the sprite multicolours from the land's $9103/$9105 for the sad or happy land, and returns the next link: line $29, handler $F1AC.
Prints string Y = 4 at offset $9B of the page in A, through $B817 (A = $45 and $49, one for each screen).
Prints string Y at offset $28 of the page in A, through $B817.
Prints string Y at offset $B1 of the page in A, through $B817.

The game-over and continue screen. Inverts the character set, prints string 4 ("GAME OVER") on both screens; when continues are left ($CF8A) puts their number, at most 9, into the '*' of "CONTINUES : *" ($B971) and prints it (string $0A) on both screens, then "CONTINUE : YES" (string 5) on screen $4400 and "CONTINUE : NO" (string 6) on screen $4800. Starts its jingle (sounds $1B-$1D through $3F0E), and runs its own raster chain ($3EC8). The stick picks the screen shown, right YES ($D018 = $1F), left NO ($2F), and fire, once released, decides: lives become 03; YES with continues left takes one ($3EAF, the wiki's continue POKE) and restarts the stage ($3B95); otherwise level 0 goes to $A547 in the land's file and any other level to the title ($CBA5).
Clears both screens to $FF with colour 0, inverts the character set back, shows screen $4800 and calls $0D1B.

Raster handler of the game-over chain, at line $36: shows the YES or NO screen (the operand $3EC9, set from the stick), calls $BDD7, the tune ($3F1E) and $193A with X = $1BEC; next link line $81, handler $3EE0.
Operand of the LDA #$FF at $3EC8: the $D018 value the game-over chain shows, $1F (screen $4400, YES) or $2F (screen $4800, NO), set by the stick at $3E5B.
Game-over chain at line $81: calls $189A and $193A with X = 3; next link line $B9, handler $3EEF.

The code-sheet protection, run once from the start-up ($199D). In play, screen $4400 row 4 column 0. In the hand-over the high byte of the STA $48EF,X at $449E.

One attempt at the code. Moves the attempt offset $44B6 on by 8 (0, 8, $10); a fourth time ($18) it jumps to $C000, which wipes memory. Decodes this attempt's grid reference (three bytes EOR $45 from $0178+offset, e.g. "D17") into the line at $475D, blanks the five code digits ($4762) and swatch colours ($465C), centres the line (one column less per narrow I or J, $4686), prints the six lines of text (strings $15-$1A through $B817), writes the colour names at $4B73, and starts the protection's raster chain ($45E7). Then it reads the keys 1-5 ($47AA/$47AF), one press at a time ($1B68): each sets the next swatch to that key's colour ($4661) and the next digit, and redraws the line. After five it compares them with the entry's code (bytes 3-7, EOR $45); a match goes on to $45A4, a mismatch blanks the line ($45DA) and tries again.
Operand of the LDY #$F8 at $44B5: the current attempt's offset in $0178 (0, 8, $10); $44A4 adds 8 each attempt and gives up at $18.

How far above his position $1BE4 the player's top is for touching objects, by the duck flag $1B62: $0F standing, $0A ducking.

The player against the 15 object slots, once a pass ($1F83). A slot counts when it shows a frame ($F4FE not $0F; or has an item frame $F8CD, or kind $FD), its state $F558 is below 4, its kind $F567 is not $FE, its layer $F6C0 matches the player's (0, or 2 when $1B4F puts the player behind the background), its X high bit is clear and its X ($F6CF) is $9C-$BB, around the player at $AC; the active flag $023C is not tested. Vertically, the player spans $1BE4 - $1B4B - $B4A6 to $1BE4 + $0F - $1B4B, against the object's Y $F6D0 (and Y + $15 for a double-height object). On a touch the overlap goes into $B58A; state 2 goes to $E4E3, state 3 (an item) to $BC15, any other to $B565.
Operand of the CMP #$FF at $B4E2: the layer ($F6C0) a slot must be on to touch the player, 0 or 2, set by $B4B3 from $1B4F.

The player touched an object of kind Y ($F567, kept in $50). With the power-up flag $1B9C set, any kind but $FF is hit at once ($C6D7); $FF goes through the stomp test. Otherwise kinds $FC and $FA always hurt the player ($B5CA) and kind $F9 jumps to $364F, which adds one to the counter $CF83-$CF85 on frames when $1B64 is 0, up to limits set by the land's $9050 ($E5BE) and by $10ED, and otherwise only plays a sound. Falling ($1B5A) with an overlap under 8 is a stomp: the bounce strength $1BAB from $342E by $1B5D, a bounce ($2EB5, A = $0D), and the object is hit ($C6D7), except kinds $FB and $F7, which then go through the walk-in test like any touch that is not a stomp. A walk-in ($B5AA) hurts when $1B54 is set; otherwise it hits the object if the player is charging ($1B52, or for kind $F7 also $1B9F), except kind $F8, which always hurts.
Operand of the LDA #$FF at $B589: how far the player's feet overlap the object (stored by $B540); under 8 counts as landing on it.

The player is hurt, unless the power-up ($1B9C) or the grace timer $1BC2 is running, or the kind is $FD, or $FF while $1B9F is set. The first touch only sets $1BB7, sets the grace count $1BC2 to $64 (counted down by $EE9E on calls when $1B68 is 1, so it lasts about $C8 calls) and plays sound $1A ($B61D, the wiki's invincibility POKE). A second touch loses the life ($B5E9).

The player loses a life (also reached from $383F when time runs out, with A = 1): $1B7F = A, the scroll speed $208C, $1BD7, the slope height $1B4B, $1BC8 and $1B4F cleared, the charge stopped ($33C9), the death frame ($EF86 + $18) in $1BE7, $1B59 = $0B, the death face patched into the frames ($BD96 with X = $0B), and sounds $18 and $19.
In the happy land, unless $1BD1 is set: flips each object's colour $F4A4 by its flash mask $F486, once a pass ($2311).

Once a pass ($1FD2), for each active slot: counts down a hit flash ($F4D1, set by $C7A7) and restores the colour and flash mask saved in $F4C2/$F495 when it ends; and for every other slot (even slots one pass, odd the next, by flipping the branch at $B667) whose $F837 is set (by $BAA1) steps its colour animation: the slot's count $F891 is decremented on each of its turns and, when it goes below 0, reloaded from $F8A0 while the next byte of the list at ($F7DD/$F7EC) is taken via the index $022D (back to the start at a byte of $10 or more) into $F4A4, so the colour steps on every ($F8A0 + 1)-th turn. A slot whose group $F846 equals $EC6F is skipped while $1BD5 is 0.
The BEQ at $B667 that skips odd or even slots; $B6B1 flips it between BEQ ($F0) and BNE ($D0) with EOR #$20 after each pass, so each slot's colour steps every second pass.

Moves the 16-bit pointer at $1BA1+X back by one 15-byte record.

Each ASCII character: $FF ends; a space moves one column; ! . , : and the narrow I, J and L draw one column wide; A-Z, the digits, ? and the others two; M and W draw a third column after them (glyphs $2A, $2B). The glyph's four cells go to the address and the row below (+$28). Used for the stage card ($3C00-$3C15), the game-over and continue screens ($3DDF-$3DE9), the protection screen ($4503, $4585), the loading screen ($CC25-$CC4A) and the stage-complete tally ($BE62, $BE79, $F27A-$F30F).
