Set to 1 after an M and $FF after a W, so the third column ($2A or $2B) is drawn next; 0 otherwise.
Cleared by $B833 for each character; no reader found.

Low bytes of the 27 strings' addresses ($B913 the high bytes): 0 $B92E, 1 $9133 (the land's stage name), 2 $B94B, 3 $B93B, 4 $B95B, 5 $B973, 6 $B982, 7 $B990, 8 $9151 (the land's LOADING line), 9 $CB90, 10 $B965, 11 $B9A0, 12 $B9AD, 13 $B9B7, 14 $B9C8, 15 $B9D5, 16 $B9DF, 17 $B9F0, 18 $B9FE, 19 $916F and 20 $9185 (the land's quota lines), 21-26 the protection's ($46C1, $46D3, $4745, $474F, $475D, $4768).
High bytes of the 27 strings' addresses.
String 0, "MAYHEM  GO!!".
String 3, "STATUS : HAPPY!".
String 2, "   STATUS : SAD".
String 4, "GAME OVER".
String 10, "CONTINUES : *"; the * at $B971 is replaced by the number left.
The * of "CONTINUES : *", replaced by '0' + the continues left (at most '9') by $3E07.
String 5, "CONTINUE : YES".
String 6, "CONTINUE : NO".
String 7, "STAGE  COMPLETE".
String 11, "TIME BONUS : *** X 100"; string 12 is its tail from $B9AD.
The *** of the time bonus line (string 12 starts here), replaced by the time left by $F28E.
String 13, "SUPER TIME BONUS".
String 14, "STAR BONUS : *** X 500"; string 15 is its tail from $B9D5.
The *** of the star bonus line (string 15), replaced by the count by $F2C9-$F2F4.
String 16, "SUPER STAR BONUS".
String 17, "SKID BONUS  : ** X 1000"; string 18 is its tail from $B9FE.
The ** of the skid bonus line (string 18), replaced by the two digits $1BF0-$1BF1 by $BE65.
Moves the objects with the background ($BA0D) when the scroll speed $208C is not 0. Called from the raster handler $21EE ($220A).

Moves every active object's X ($F6CF, every other byte) by the scroll speed $1BD7, against the scroll direction $1B3F, so objects keep their place in the land. Works through the three bands of five slots from slot 14 down; when an X passes a page edge it flips the slot's X high bit in its band's byte ($F474-$F476, the operands at $BA48/$BA4E stepping down from $F476) and marks the page step ($BA6F). Also called from $1CF7.
Operand (low byte) of the LDA $F476 at $BA47: the current band's X high-bit byte, $76 down to $74 ($BA0F, $BA63).
Operand (low byte) of the STA $F476 at $BA4D, stepped with $BA48.
Operand of the LDX #$FF at $BA56: the slot number kept by $BA28 across the page step.
The current slot's bit in its band's X high-bit byte, $10 down to $01 ($BA1B, $BA58).
Slots left in the current band, 4 down to 0 ($BA20, $BA5E).
Sets slot X's page step $F6A2 to $FF or 1 for the object that just crossed a page edge, by the scroll direction $1B3F and the slot's $F693.
Counts slot X's page counter $F6B1 up or down after the object itself crossed a page edge, by its direction (bit 7 of $F53A) and $F693. Called from $C34A.

Gives slot X the colour list of object type Y from the land's tables: address $96B3+Y / $96C3+Y into $F7DD/$F7EC, delay $96D3+Y into $F8A0; resets the list index $022D to $FF, the delay count $F891 to 0 and sets $F837. Called from $C822 and $E522; $BAB0 is entered from $BF9A with the delay in A.

Copies the 15 slots' X/Y positions ($F6CF-$F6EC) to $F4E0-$F4FD and the three bands' X high-bit bytes ($F474-$F476, low five bits) to $F483-$F485, for the sprite multiplexer ($C0DC, $C01C, $C07C) to read in the next frame. Called from the raster handler $22BA.
How many times $E1AF shifts the characters at $7FDD-$7FF3, by $1B68: 1 or 3, a loop run twice or four times (read at $E1AC).
Y positions of the stage card's eight sprites, written by $F1C4 and read by $E1E9 (0 as loaded).

The stage card's motion table, $50 entries ($BAE7-$BB36) read backwards as $BAE6+X by $ED6D while the card counter $BB37 runs down from $50: signed steps with bit 7 for upward ($82, $81, 0, 1, 2 ... up to 4, then $8F, $8E ...), a bounce.
The stage card's counter: $3BF5 sets it to $50, $ED6A counts it down a frame at a time with the bounce at $BAE6, and the card accepts fire only when it is 0 ($3D6C).
Colours for the player's sprite 7 ($1BE8) in the six steps after collecting an item, one every third frame ($1B9A counts 6 down, $BCD3).
Colours for the player's sprite 6 (the operand at $E44B) in the same six steps.

Colours for sprite 7 ($1BE8) cycled during the power-up, eight steps ($BD1B); $1B9C counts the power-up down once every third frame ($BCF6), so $FD lasts about 760 frames, more while an item flash ($1B9A) holds the count.
Colours for sprite 6 ($E44B) cycled during the power-up.
Not referenced: bytes that decode as LDX #0/1/2, LDY #0 and JSR (or JMP) $0C84 three times, starting effect 0 on each of the three effect channels.

Item effect 3 (the jump table at $F994/$F99D), also entered from $2B69: starts the power-up, $1B9C = $FD frames. If it was not running: the effect sprite ($33F4 with A = 1, which starts sprite 4's puff and plays no sound), $1B9B = 7, $BB9D, $1479 = 0, and then, when $1BC6 is set, it returns there; otherwise $1B97 is saved in $1B99. Then (also when the power-up was already running) $1BC1 = $1E ($3648), the touch counter $1BB7 cleared ($387D), $1B97 = 8 and $E4D0. While $1B9C runs the player hits every object he touches ($B565) and cannot be hurt ($B5CA).
Clears $1B6B and $1B6C.

Installs the play-time raster chain: the game's own interrupt exit ($1884), then $1809 with the handler $F1AC, $01 = $35 (KERNAL out, I/O in) and carry set (the vector at $FFFE/$FFFF pointing at $1862); $1809 sets the first interrupt at raster line $F9. Called from the start-up $1975 and the stage card $3CAD.

Points the character animation code at $2337-$2354 at the land's two animated characters, $9023 and $9024: each becomes the address of its eight bytes in the character set ($BBE4) and is written into three operands each ($233B/$2353/$234C and $233E/$2350/$2337, high bytes after them). Called from $B7C0 and $E54F.

A = character code; returns its address in the character set, $7800 + 8 * A, low byte in A, high byte in X, using $1921/$1922 as work bytes. Character 0 gives $1921 itself (A = $21, X = $19), a harmless target.

The player touched an item (an object in state 3, $B553): marks its record in the land's list ($CB02), frees the slot ($C417), starts the six-step flash ($1B9A = 6, a step every third frame) unless the power-up runs, plays sound 9, scores 200 points (500 in the sad land once the quota flag $36F3 is set), then jumps to the item's effect: the land's $9075 maps the slot's item number $F8DC to an effect 0-8, whose address comes from $F994/$F99D (0 $BC55, 1 $35F3, 2 $36D2, 3 $BB69, 4 $3636, 5 $36ED, 6 $CB4B, 7 $10C1, 8 $10D5).
Operand of the LDX #$FF at $BC3D: the slot number, stored by $BC15.
Operand (low byte) of the JMP at $BC52: the effect's address, from $F994+effect.
Operand (high byte) of the JMP at $BC52, from $F99D+effect.
Item effect 0: increments $1BEB, which lets fire start the charge in the player's movement ($3326).
The stage card's first row of glyph codes, $EF-$F2 four times, copied to screen $463C by $3C32.
The stage card's second row, $F3-$F6 four times, copied to $4664 by $3C3E.
The stage card's third row, $F7-$FA four times, copied to $468C by $3C4A.
The stage card's fourth row, $FB and $FC alternately, copied to $46B4 by $3C56.
Starts any sound effects requested this frame ($BC9F), then plays one frame of the effects ($0A70). Called from $1CF4, $1FDD, the tune steps at $3F31 and the stage-complete handler at $F361.

Starts the effects requested on the three effect channels: when $1B85, $1B86 or $1B87 is set it is cleared and effect $1B88, $1B89 or $1B8A is started on channel 0, 1 or 2 ($0C84). One request per call, channel 0 first.
The test for channel 2's request. $12AB rewrites its first byte to RTS ($60, as in play) or back to LDA ($AD), so channel 2 is not used for effects while the music needs that voice.

The player's colour flashes, every third frame: while $1B9A counts the six steps after an item (on frames with $1B67 = 0), sprite 7's colour $1BE8 and sprite 6's (the operand at $E44B) come from $BB38/$BB3E; otherwise, during the power-up ($1B9C, counted down here on frames with $1B67 = 1, and not while the item flash runs) they cycle through $BB44/$BB4C with $1B9B, and when it ends they return to $0A and 0, $1B6D/$1B6E to $0F, $1479 to 4, $1B97 to $1B99, and $E4D0 runs. Called from $1F61.
Index of the last byte of the counter sprite's caption at $F9A6 for the sad ($17) and happy ($2F) land: the sad and happy captions are $F9A6-$F9BD and $F9BE-$F9D5.
Index of the last time digit in the land's block, from $9044: 2 for the sad land ($9044-$9046), 5 for the happy land ($9047-$9049).

Sets the time $CF86-$CF88 from the land's start time for the sad or happy land (Y = $1BEC: $9044-$9046 or $9047-$9049), and copies the counter sprite's 24-byte caption for that state from $F9A6 into sprite block 4 ($4109). Called from $3B9D and $E57E.

One frame of the player's death leap ($1ECF), unless it has finished ($1B80): adds the step $344E + $1BC8 to his Y $1BE4 (never above $34), moving the index on until the step is 8; once he is below $F4 sets $1B80 = $28. Then $EF93 with Y by the index: 0 below $10, 2 for $10-$13, 1 from $14 (the leap's rising, top and falling frames).

Patches six consecutive bytes (two sprite rows) in each of the player's frames, $58A1-$58A6 and $5221-$5226, with the face set ending at X ($BDA9, $BDB5): X = 5 the first set, $0B the second, the death face ($B611). Also called from $1D52.
Two sets of six bytes for $58A1 (the second is the death face).
Two sets of six bytes for $5221.

Takes a life off the two-digit lives counter $CF81-$CF82 and sets $3887 for the redraw. When the units are 0 it decrements the tens and leaves the units 0, so 10 lives become 00, not 09; 00 is the last life and the next loss makes $CF81 $FF, game over. Called from $1FA4.

Once a frame (the end of $20F8, and other raster chains): counts $1B64 round 5-0, $1B65 4-0, $1B66 3-0 and $1B67 2-0, and flips $1B68 between 0 and 1. The rest of the game uses them to act every second to sixth frame.
In the sad land only, runs $BE0D; called from the play loop ($2060).

Lightning, if the land's $903D is set: every third frame counts $1BED down; at 0 it starts the background flash ($20E2 = $11, the colours from $BE38), sets the next interval from a pseudo-random step of $1BEE ($1BEE x 4 + $51 + $1BEE, one more when the first addition carries; low seven bits) and plays sound $20. The wiki's unlimited-lives POKE at $BE15 lands on the BNE here, which only stops the lightning; its address must be for another version.

The lightning's background colours, read backwards as $BE38 + count by $20E1 while the count at $20E2 runs down from $11 ($BE49 first, $BE39 last): 1, 0, 1, $0C, $0B, 1, $0F, $0C, $0B, 0, 1, 1, $0F, $0F, $0C, $0B, 0. $BE38 itself is the last byte of the JMP before it.
The seventeen entries of the lightning's colour sequence proper, $BE39 (count 1, shown last) to $BE49 (count $11, shown first); the label at $BE38 names the base the count is added to.
Ends one part of the end-of-stage tally: $1B4D = 0, $1B3D on to the next part.
Prints "SKID BONUS" (string $11 at $46A9) and its two digits ($BE65), or, when the skid count $1BEF is 0, sets $1B54 so the skid part is skipped. Called from $F318.
Puts the skid count's two digits $1BF0-$1BF1 into string $12 ($B9FE) and prints it at $46BF.
Scores event Y ($350B) and plays the tally's tick, sound $2B.

The end-of-stage tally, a frame at a time, after $F302 has shown "STAGE COMPLETE". $1B3D picks the part and $1B4D counts frames in it. Part 0, time: from frame $3C, every third frame one unit of time ($37F8, redrawn by $F286) for 100 points, until the time is 000; with $1BA9 set it gives event $0E (100,000) once instead. Part 1, stars: from frame $28, one off the counter $CF83-$CF85 ($370F, redrawn by $F2EC) for 500 points each until 000; with $1B76 set (the super star bonus, $F2AA) one award of 1,000,000 instead. Part 2, skid: from frame $28, one off the skid count $1BF0-$1BF1 per step for 1000 points while $1BEF lasts, skipped when $1B54 is set. On frame $23 of part 0 and frame $14 of parts 1 and 2 it increments $1B8B, $1B8C and $1B8D, which switch on the stage-complete handler's colour stripes in rows 10-12, 14-15 and 17-18 ($F3CC-$F3FC). Then fire ($DC00 bit 4) loads the next land ($CBAD). Each frame redraws the score and lives ($BF61).
Redraws the score ($3578) and lives ($3892) and, in the tally's last part ($1B3D = 3), waits for fire to go on to $CBAD.
Y = the land's object type $9075+Y, then falls into $BF7F. Called from $C9CB.
Gives slot X colour list Y from $B6BA/$B6C3: the list's address into $F7DD/$F7EC, its first byte into the colour $F4A4, and its delay $B6CC into $F8A0 ($BAB0). Called from $C9C6.
Operand (low byte) of the LDA $FFFF at $BF91: the colour list's address, set by $BF85.
Operand (high byte) of the LDA at $BF91, set by $BF8E.

Used by the land's scene code (Jellyland calls it from $93A4): while the countdown in its own operand ($BF9E) is not 0 it only counts it down; at 0 it shows six sprites in place of the panel: frames $D0-$D2 twice ($10DB) on both screens, colours from the land's $96D9-$96DE, positions from $10E1, sprite set-up 4 ($1A56).
Operand of the LDA #$FF at $BF9D: frames left before $BF9D shows its sprites; $BFA1 counts it down (0 in play, $FF as loaded).
The sound effect $3366 plays when the charge starts, by $1BB6: 1, or $10 when $1BB6 is set.
The sound effect $341E plays, by $1BB6: 2, or $11.
The sound effect $2D7F reads, by $1BB6: $0A, or $13.

A 39-byte buffer ($BFCF-$BFF5) for one row of colour RAM: $28E6 saves row 14 here (X = $26 down to 0) and $2978 puts it back into row 15 while the colour rows are moved down; that second loop ends at X = 1, so the first byte (column 0) is saved but never put back.
Ten bytes after the colour buffer (0, $FF, 1, $4A, $FF, $4F, 1, 3, $CF, $FD) with no reader found.
The protection's punishment after a third wrong code ($44B2): stores 0 at $040A and $400A, then steps both STA operands up a byte at a time, for ever, until it overwrites itself.
Operand (low byte) of the STA $040A at $C002, incremented by $C008.
Operand (high byte) of the STA $040A, incremented at $C010 when the low byte wraps.
Operand (low byte) of the STA $400A at $C005, incremented by $C00B.
Operand (high byte) of the STA $400A, incremented at $C013.

JMP $CE66 (restart a game with the font swapped back). The ending jumps here (JMP $C019 at its $5A13); nothing in the engine, the intro or the lands names $C019, and the JMP $C002 before it never falls through.

Sprite multiplexer for the second band of objects (slots 5-9) on sprites 0-4: X high bits from $F484, and for each sprite n (0-4) not skipped: hidden (Y 0) when $F5B7 is 0, otherwise its colour $F4A9, X/Y from the latched positions $F4EA/$F4EB and frame $F503 into both screens' pointers; then the band's multicolour, priority (with $1B4F), Y and X expansion bytes $F478/$F47B/$F47E/$F481 and multicolour 1 from $1B8C. The skip flag is entry n of $F5C1-$F5C5, one per sprite column shared by all bands (written at spawn from record byte 8 bit 2 by whichever object last took that column, $E9DC); a set flag leaves the sprite as band 0 placed it. Called from the raster handlers whose JSR $C0DB the land's band table points here ($29B0, $90B0); $E5B4 turns it off and on by writing RTS or LDA to its first byte.
Sprite multiplexer for the third band of objects (slots 10-14), as $C01C with $F485, $F5BC, $F4AE, $F4F4/$F4F5, $F508, $F479/$F47C/$F47F/$F482 and $1B8D.
The RTS a band handler's JSR points at when that band shows no objects ($29EC entry 0).

Sprite multiplexer for the first band of objects (slots 0-4), from the bottom handler $20F8 each frame: as $C01C with $F483, $F5B2, $F4A4, $F4E0/$F4E1, $F4FE, $F477/$F47A/$F47D/$F480 (X expansion cleared first) and multicolour 0 and 1 from $1B8E and $1B8B, then jumps to $F41D. A slot whose $F5B2 is 0 is hidden (Y 0); there is no skip test in this band.
The sound effects' addresses for $0C84 (read as $C144+Y and $C145+Y with Y = effect * 2): 35 effects of 20 bytes each, $0D2E, $0D42 ... $0FD6.
High bytes of the effect addresses, read by $0C94 as $C145+Y.

Moves the 15 object slots one frame (called from the play loop at $1FBA). For slot X it keeps $45 = 2X (index of its X/Y pair at $F6CF/$F6D0), $82 = its bit in its band of five and $85 = the band. Inactive slots, state 5, and a slot whose group $F846 equals $EC6F while $1BD5 is 0 are skipped; states 3 and 4 (any state from 3 but 5) skip the horizontal step and go straight to the page step. A slot without a parent ($F675) whose page counter $F6B1 reaches 3 has left the land and goes ($C3DF). With $F61B set the object homes in on the player's X ($AC) a pixel a frame, its offset $F648 bounded by $F62A/$F639; otherwise it follows its horizontal script at ($D9,X/$E8,X) through the position $0200,X. A script byte is $FE (wait here), $FD (change layer, $C55A), $10 (start again; a child re-reads its parent, $C56D), any other byte with bit 6 set (repeat: the low six bits are a count kept in $F51C and the script goes back that many times, so the stretch runs count + 1 times; $3F repeats for ever, and so does 0, which is stored again each time; the next byte is how many bytes to go back), or a move: with bit 7 set left by the low four bits, otherwise right (by the whole byte, not only its low four bits). Moving past a page edge flips the slot's X high bit and counts the page ($BA8A). Then the page step from scrolling ($F6A2), the off-screen test ($C362: an object far enough off either edge, by the scroll and its own direction, is removed or, as a child, hidden), and the vertical script ($C42A).
Operand of the CMP #$FF at $C2BC: bit 7 of the slot's last direction ($F53A), stored by $C2AD, compared with the new move's direction to see whether it turned.
Operand of the SBC #$FF at $C305: how many bytes a repeat byte sends the horizontal script back, read from the script by $C2FE.
Operand of the CMP #$FF at $C39F: the scroll speed negated ($C399), compared with the object's own speed to see whether it outruns the scroll.
An object has left the screen or the land: a child of another ($F675) is only hidden (frame $0F, $F936 = $FE); any other is freed ($C417) together with every other slot of its group ($F846).
Operand of the CPX #$FF at $C3FE: the slot that left, stored by $C3F9, skipped while its group is freed.
Frees slot X: frame $0F (blank), state $F558 = 5, $023C and $F5B2 = 0. Called from $BC1B, $C3F1, $C409, $C95D and $EA1D.

The vertical half of $C18A for slot X: its script at ($F6ED,X/$F6FC,X) through the position $020F,X, in the same byte format (bit 7 up, the repeat count in $F52B), moving its Y $F6D0. $10 starts it again unless $F936 is negative (a hidden child).
Operand of the CMP #$FF at $C479: bit 7 of the slot's last vertical direction ($F549), stored by $C466.
Operand of the SBC #$FF at $C4CD: how many bytes a repeat byte sends the vertical script back ($C4C6).

Clears the object system for a new stage ($1E11): all three bands' X high-bit, X-expansion and Y-expansion bytes ($F474-$F476, $F480-$F482, $F47D-$F47F) to $1F, and for each slot the frame ($0F), position, latched position, fade, state, active flag, repeat counts, kind, parent and group.
Script byte $FD: flips slot X between the two layers ($F6C0 EOR 2) and its sprite-behind-background bit in its band's $F47A byte.

Slot X is a child of slot $F657,X. When the parent is in state 3 or more the child is hidden (frame $0F) and $F936 = $FF; when the parent's $F666 is 0, only $F936 = $FF (the frame is left). Otherwise $F936 = 2; if the parent holds on a script code 2 ($F684 set) that hold is cleared and the parent's script index $021E moved on one, past the code; and the child takes the parent's page, page step, $F693 and direction, the horizontal script for that direction ($F7FB/$F80A or $F819/$F828), its X high bit and position, and restarts its scripts and colour list ($F909, $F52B, $020F, $022D, $F891 cleared). When the parent has a group ($F846), other than $EC6F while $1BD5 is 0, every other slot of that group restarts its animation ($C67D).
Operand of the CPX #$FF at $C64A: the parent's slot, stored by $C645.
Blanks slot X's frame, then falls into $C662. Called from $C817.
Gives slot X the animation of type Y from the land's tables: $F927 = Y, script address $94AE+Y / $94EE+Y into $F70B/$F71A, $952E+Y into $F864, $F684 = 0; then $C67D. Called from $E51D.
Restarts slot X's animation: $021E = $FF, $F855 and $F873 = 0.
X = the byte at $0039 (LDX $0039), then $C68D. Called from $EC11.
Splits slot X (0-14) into its band Y (0-2) and its place in the band X (0-4).
Kills slot X ($C7C3) and every other active slot in state 0 of the same group ($F846), unless of kind $FC.
Operand of the CPX #$FF at $C6B4: the slot $C6A4 started from, stored by $C6AF.
Operand of the CMP #$FF at $C6CC: the group number, stored by $C6AC.

The player hit object X ($B5A7), with its kind in $50 and the charge flag $1B52 in Y; nothing happens in state 3 or more. Kinds $FF, $FC and $F7 cannot be hurt: unless $1B9F or the power-up $1B9C is set they only make sound 3 (with $2FFB+1), and a charging hit sets $1B9F. Kind $F8 dies at once ($C72F). Kind $FD bounces the player ($2EB5 with A = $20) and plays sound $0E. Any other kind is the object's strength: charging or with the power-up it dies; otherwise the stomp's strength $1BAB is taken from it, and if that leaves 0 or more it lives on weaker ($C735), else it dies ($C6A4, then sounds 4 and 5 at $CB42).
Stores A as slot X's new kind (the strength left) and gives the same kind to every other active slot of its group ($F846, the operand at $C754), then flashes it if it is not already flashing ($C768).
Operand of the LDA #$FF at $C753: the new strength, stored by $C73D, given to the group's other slots.

With Z clear (Y = 1) only plays sound 3 with the parameter $2FFB+Y ($1325). Otherwise, when slot X is not already flashing, starts the white hit flash ($C7A7) on it and on the active, state-0 slots of its group, then plays sound 3 with $2FFB as the parameter.
Operand of the CPX #$FF at $C780: the slot hit, stored by $C777.
Operand of the LDY #$FF at $C79A: Y kept across the group loop ($C77A).
Starts slot X's hit flash: keeps its colour in $F4C2 and flash mask in $F495, sets the flash timer $F4D1 = 4, the colour to white (1) and the mask to 0. $B645 restores them.

Slot X dies: unless already in state 4, sets state 4 and clears its flash masks $F486/$F495. Then it chooses what the object turns into: from the low nibble of $F8AF (4 or more: an item, its number less 4 in $F8DC), $F8EB (set: item $0A whatever the mood) and the sad/happy flag, an item frame for $F8CD from the land's $905D (0, no item, in the sad land unless $F8EB is set) and the animation number $C816 (the low nibble, 0, or the land's $9069 entry), which $C65D starts. Then the colour list from the high nibble of $F8AF ($BAA1), the object's points ($3508), its scripts cleared, and by $F8BE the multicolour bit and a double-width (X 12 left) or double-height (Y 21 up) sprite.
Operand of the LDY at $C815: the script number that $C65D starts for the object here, written by $C7DC (the low nibble of $F8AF) $C7F9 (0) or $C808 (the land's $9069 entry).
Operand of the LDA at $C874, written by $C85B with the slot's $F8BE: when its bit 7 is clear the slot's multicolour bit in $F477 is cleared.
Operand of the LDA at $C883, written by $C847 with bit 5 of $F8BE: when set the slot's double-width bit in $F480 ($D01D) is set (and $C84C has moved X 12 left).
Operand of the LDA at $C890, written by $C860 with bit 6 of $F8BE: when set the slot's double-height bit in $F47D ($D017) is set (and $C865 has moved Y 21 up).
Operand of the LDX at $C89D: the slot number, saved by $C825 so it survives the calls and is reloaded on the way out.

Runs one step of every object's animation script; called once a pass from $1FC2. Takes the 15 object slots X = 0-14 but only every other one: the BEQ at $C8A7 is flipped to BNE (EOR #$20 on its opcode, $C93C) after each pass, so even and odd slots alternate. A slot is skipped when it is empty ($023C), in state 3 or 5 ($F558), waiting out its start delay ($F936: counted down, negative = frozen), or in group $F846 = $EC6F while $1BD5 is 0. In state 0, unless $F8FA is $C0, $CA8B first picks the script for its direction. The frame delay $F855 counts down and reloads from $F864; when it runs out, and $F684 is 0, the next script byte is read from ($F70B/$F71A) at index $021E: 0 restarts the script; 1 ends it ($C955); 2 holds on the current byte ($F684 = 2); 5 zeroes the delay; 3 and 4 (only while happy, or with $F5A3 set; otherwise they are frame numbers) swap the value in $F567 with one from the script, saving and restoring it through $F576; $40-$5F repeats a stretch ($CA68); anything else is a sprite frame number, stored in $F4FE. If any object turned into an item this pass ($CA07) it plays sound effect 8 ($1352).
The branch that picks even or odd slots: $C93C flips its opcode between BEQ ($F0) and BNE ($D0) with EOR #$20 after every pass of $C8A0.

Script code 1. If the slot has no item frame in $F8CD its record in the land's object list is marked ($CB02) and the slot is freed ($C417); if bit 4 of $F5D0 is set the slot is freed without marking. Otherwise the object becomes that item: frame $F8CD, sprite expansion bits cleared for the slot (remembered in the operands at $C9D2/$C9F8), multicolour bit set while sad, its colour list chosen by $F8EB (list 5 through $BF7F when set, else the land's $9075 entry through $BF7B), the position moved to the centre of the old sprite (+12 across if it was double width, with the X high bit flipped on a carry; +21 down if double height) and state 3. In Jellyland, while $1BEB is set, an object whose $9075 entry is 0 is marked and removed instead.
Operand of the LDX at $C9AB: the slot number, saved by $C96D around the call to $C68D.
Operand of the LDA at $C9D1: the slot's double-width bit, saved by $C97F before it is cleared; when set the item is moved 12 right.
Operand of the LDX at $C9E5: the slot's bit number within its band (slot mod 5), saved by $C973 for flipping the X high bit in $F474.
Operand of the LDY at $C9E7: the slot's band (slot div 5), saved by $C976.
Operand of the LDA at $C9F7: the slot's double-height bit, saved by $C991 before it is cleared; when set the item is moved 21 down.
Script codes other than 0, 1, 2 and 5: 3 and 4 when allowed (see $C8A0), the repeat command $40-$5F, and otherwise a sprite frame number written to $F4FE.

Script command $40 + n, d: repeats the stretch before it. On first meeting it sets the counter $F873 to n and jumps back without counting (with n = 0 it counts at once, to $FF); each later meeting decrements the counter and jumps back while it is not 0, so the stretch runs n + 1 times, or 256 times with n = 0. The jump goes d bytes back from the byte d (the frame there is shown at once); when the counter runs out the script continues after the two bytes, whose index was kept in $F882.

For an object in state 0: chooses its script from the six loaded at spawn. Unless $F8FA is $40, the first time ($F918 = 0) it takes the script at $F729/$F738 when $F549 is negative, else $F747/$F756. Then, when $F8FA is 0 or $40, once ($F909 = 0) by $F53A: bit 7 set with a low nibble gives $F765/$F774, bit 7 clear with a low nibble $F783/$F792, a zero nibble $F7A1/$F7B0 (bit 7 set) or $F7BF/$F7CE.
Points slot X's animation at the script A (low) / Y (high): stores them in $F70B/$F71A, sets the index $021E to $FF so the next step reads byte 0, and clears the repeat counter $F873.

If the slot's $F5D0 is non-zero, marks the object's record in the land's object list (pointer kept in $F5DF/$F5EE at spawn): byte 10 gets bit 7 when bits 5-6 of $F5D0 are %10, otherwise bit 4 unless $F5D0 bit 4 is set. The spawner $E75E skips records whose byte 10 has bit 7 set, except when the low nibble of byte 9 is $0B or more ($E78D-$E795 jump past that test), and $E595 clears bits 4 and 7 of every record when a land starts. Called from $C95A and $BC18.

Unreached as far as found: no JSR, JMP or address in the engine, the intro, the lands or the ending names $CB30. Reads keyboard row select $FD (read_key_row $1AD6) and compares the column bits with $7F, so Z is set when only column 7 of that row is down. A leftover.
Restarts slot X's animation script from its first byte ($C67D: index $FF, delay and repeat counter 0) and clears $F909 and $F684. Called from $C21F, $C23C, $C256, $C2C0.
Requests sound effects 4 and 5 through $1352 (X = 4, then 5); reached by JMP from $C732.

Item effect 6: entry 6 of the dispatch table $F994/$F99D, reached through the JMP at $BC52. Sets $1BAA to $14 and $1BC0 to $1E. While $1BAA is non-zero the time tick at $37F8 decrements it instead of the time, so the clock stands still for 20 ticks. Its RTS is the byte at $CB55, which doubles as entry 0 of the mask table there.
Masks that clear the lowest x bits: entry x (1-7) is $FF shifted left x times ($FE, $FC ... $80). Read only by the loading bar at $CE0D with x = 1-7; entry 0 is the RTS of $CB4B.
Single-bit masks, entry x = 1 << x ($01-$80). Read throughout the object code to set an object's bit in the per-band sprite attribute bytes ($F474-$F485), with x = slot mod 5 from $C68D.
The complements of $CB5D: entry x = all bits but bit x ($FE-$7F). Used to clear an object's bit in the per-band sprite attribute bytes ($F474-$F485).
Y = which group of ten X falls in: 0 for X < 10, 1 for X < 20, 2 otherwise. Called from $B4E8.

Twenty-two sprite Y coordinates eight lines apart, $35 + 8n: $2D59 copies entry $1BE6 into $1BE4 (the coordinate $E2F0 and $E426 read as Mayhem's height), so it turns a character row into a sprite line.

"LOADING : JELLYLAND", ASCII, $FF-terminated: string 9 of the print routine $B817 (pointer tables $B8F8/$B913). The loader prints it for the first land; later lands print string 8, the "LOADING :" line at $9151 of the land just finished.

Fire-button latch of the "insert side B" prompt ($CD02-$CD13): cleared while fire is held, set to 1 when fire is let go after a press. It is 0 in the image as loaded, so the first time the prompt appears the loader retries after the delay without waiting for fire (nothing else writes it).

Start a game from the first land. Entered by JMP from the protection screen ($45D7), from $3E9E (game over) and through $CE66. Banks every ROM and the I/O out ($01 = $34) to run $D76E, which resets the level index to $FF and the quota strings, then falls into $CBAD.

Load the next land and start it ($BF78 jumps here after a stage is won). Increments the level index $CF89, silences ($0D1B), clears the stack page to $FF and $0002-$00FF to 0, blanks the screen and sprites, sets screen $4400 with characters at $5000 ($D018 = $15), swaps pages through $3F54 (3: $7800-$7FFF with $5000-$57FF, 4: $D800-$DFFF with $7800-$7FFF, 6: the drive code at $D000 with $4000), builds the file name from $CF10 and the level index ("LA"-"LE", "CF" for the ending), prints the loading screen through $B817 (string 9 or 8, then the two quota lines from $916F and $9185 unless the ending is next), turns the screen on and adds a life ($3866, at $CC55). Then, with the KERNAL in ($01 = $36), opens the file through the KERNAL's serial routines (SETLFS, SETNAM, LISTEN, SECOND, then $F3F6 in ROM to send the name, TALK, TKSA, ACPTR). A status of $42 in $90 at $CC5C would go straight to the prompt, but $90 was zeroed with the rest of zero page at $CBC6; if the drive does not answer, or the file is not found, it shows "INSERT SIDE B AND PRESS FIRE" ($CCF5). Otherwise it uploads the drive code with M-W, starts it with M-E at $07AB and receives the file into $5A00-$B0FF with $CE6C, moving the loading bar one pixel a block. Afterwards it restores the screen and swaps pages again (5 and 6) and starts the land: Jellyland through $F45E (the land's own code at $A547), the other lands through $E54F and $3B3F, the ending at $5A00.

The disk prompt. Writes the 28 glyphs at $CEE1 to the bottom row of screen $4400 ($47C6), waits for the fire button to be pressed and released ($CBA4, joystick port 2 bit 4; the first time the prompt appears it does not wait, since $CBA4 starts at 0), waits about 65,000 loop passes, then retries the load from $CC65.

The file was found: clears the prompt row, uploads the 256-byte drive routine from $4000 (where swap 6 put the copy kept at $D000) into drive RAM $0700-$07FF in eight M-W commands of 32 bytes, starts it with M-E $07AB, builds the 256-byte decoding table at $4B00 from $CEAD (each entry repeated eight times), and receives the file: four bytes before the first data byte (the first block's link and the file's load address), two link bytes before each later block's 254 data bytes, stored from $5A00 upward through the patched STA at $CDC3 until the high byte reaches $CF0C ($B1). Every block moves the loading bar ($CDDB): blocks 1-7 of a cell each clear one more pixel column (from the right) of rows 1-6 of glyph $BE with $CB55; on the eighth the cell becomes glyph $BF and the bar moves one cell left ($CF16, $CF17). The first cell's count starts at 1 ($CC7B), so its first block clears two columns and its seventh moves the bar on.
Low byte of the fast loader's store address: the operand of the STA at $CDC3, incremented after each byte by $CDC8.
High byte of the fast loader's store address: set to $5A from $CF0D by $CDAB, incremented at $CDCD and compared with $CF0C ($B1) to end the load.

After the last byte: reads 256 more bytes from the drive and discards them, switches the I/O back in ($01 = $35), waits for raster line 0, restores the play-time display set-up and the pages swapped before the load (5: $D800-$DFFF with $5000; 6: the drive code back to $D000), and branches by level index: 0 Jellyland via $F45E, 5 the ending at $5A00 with a fresh stack, others via $E54F then $3B3F with A = 0.
Reached by JMP from $C019: swaps $D800-$DFFF with $7800-$7FFF ($3F52, swap 0) and starts a new game at $CBA5.

Receives one byte from the drive's fast-load routine. Raises the line in $A4 on CIA 2 port A, waits for the drive to raise DATA (bit 7), waits for a raster position away from the lines whose low bits are 2 or 3 (bad lines) once below line $31, drops the line ($A5) and, after ten NOPs, reads $DD00 four times on a fixed cycle count; each value read indexes the table at $4B00 offset by 0, 8, 16 and 24 in turn, and the four results ORed together are the byte, returned in A. Ends with CLI.

The 32 values from which $CD91 builds the decoding table at $4B00 (each repeated eight times). Each group of eight belongs to one state of the CLK and DATA lines in a read of $DD00 (group 0 both low, 1 CLK high, 2 DATA high, 3 both high), and its first four entries are the bits that state gives in the first, second, third and fourth read ($A0/$50/$0A/$05, $20/$10/$02/$01, $80/$40/$08/$04, and 0), since $CE6C indexes the table at offsets 0, 8, 16 and 24. The rest are $FF or 0, for port values that do not occur.
Opens the drive's command channel (LISTEN device $BA, secondary $6F) and sends "M-"; the caller sends "W" or "E" and the rest.
"INSERT SIDE B AND PRESS FIRE" in the loading font's glyph numbers: $90 + the letter's place in the alphabet, $FF a space. Copied to the bottom screen row by $CCF5.
"LOADING . . . ", ASCII, $FF-terminated. No reader was found by absolute address, and it is not one of the print routine's pointers at $B8F8/$B913.
$B1: the page at which the fast loader stops (the land occupies $5A00-$B0FF). Written by $CC10, read at $CDD3.
$5A: the first page the fast loader writes, copied into the STA at $CDC3 by $CDA8. Written by $CC0B.

The two-letter file name passed to the KERNAL's SETNAM: the first letter from $CF10 (L or C), the second "A" + level index; so "LA"-"LE" are the lands and "CF" the ending. Written by $CC06/$CC17; "**" as loaded.
Second letter of the file name: "A" + level index, written by $CC17.
The first letter of each file name by level index: "L" for the five lands, "C" for the ending (index 5).
The loading bar's current cell, 10 down to 0 (screen $4577 + cell). Set to 10 by $CC80, stepped by $CDE3-$CDF5.
Blocks received within the current cell of the loading bar, 0-7: 1 at the start ($CC7B), 0 after each move to a new cell ($CE03), counted up by $CDDB.

A rising table of 96 small steps (0, then 1s, 2s, 3s ... up to 8 at $CF76): $237E adds entry $1B81 to the player's X $1BE3 as $1B81 counts down, and $3392 reads the table one entry on as the scroll speed for the speed counter $1B51, so it is a curve of horizontal speeds (the big steps at the top entries, small near 0). $CF77 is cleared with the score by $E52D.
The same curve read one entry on: $3392 returns entry Y + 1 of $CF18 in X, halved (at least 1) when $1BB6 is set.
Written only by $E536 (the new-game clear, X = 0) in the loop that clears the score from $CF78; it is also the last entry of the jump curve $CF18.

The score, nine decimal digits one per byte, most significant first ($CF80 the units). $350B adds an amount from $34E7 at a digit from $34F7 with carry, and calls $3636 (a life and its sound) when the amount is added at the millions digit $CF7A or a carry rolls the hundred-thousands digit $CF7B over from 9; an amount added at $CF7B itself (event $0E, 100,000) that carries into the millions gives no life (from $3545 the carry starts at $CF7A, past the test at $355A). $3578 redraws each digit that differs from its copy at $CF8C. Cleared by $E52D at a new game.
Score digit for the ten millions (second of nine at $CF78-$CF80).
Score digit for the millions: an amount added to it, or a carry that rolls $CF7B over from 9, gives an extra life through $3636 (a carry out of an amount added at $CF7B does not; see $CF78).
Score digit for the hundred thousands.
Score digit for the ten thousands.
Score digit for the thousands.
Score digit for the hundreds.
Score digit for the tens.
Score digit for the units, the last of the nine at $CF78; drawn at sprite position $AF by $35E0. Not a lives digit.

Lives, tens digit (the units are $CF82). $3866 adds a life; $BDC1 takes one (decrementing this digit at $BDCE when the units are 0); $3E77 sets it to 0 with the units to 3; $1EB6 sets it to $FF when the player quits with Q, which $3BAC reads as game over (negative). Drawn by $3892 at sprite position $EE.
Lives, units digit: 3 at a new game ($E547) and at $3E7C. $3866 adds a life with a decimal carry into $CF81; $BDC1 takes one ($BDC7-$BDD3, borrowing from $CF81 and leaving 0). Also read by $10EF.

The count of magic dust still needed (sad) or of stars still needed (happy), three decimal digits $CF83-$CF85, most significant first. Set from the land's $903E-$9040 at the start of a land ($E583, X = 2) and from $9041-$9043 when the land turns happy ($3BC6, X = 5); $370F counts it down, $3675 up; drawn by $3762 at sprite positions $2D-$2F. On the stage-complete screen $F29D tests it for 000 and otherwise rewrites it as the land's $904A-$904C minus itself (the stars over the quota, $F2D8), which the tally then counts down ($BEEA-$BEFC).
Middle digit of the count in $CF83-$CF85.
Last digit of the count in $CF83-$CF85.

The time left, three decimal digits $CF86-$CF88, most significant first. Set by $BD37 from the land's $9044-$9046 (sad) or $9047-$9049 (happy); $37E9 counts it down one unit each time $1BEA has counted $4A down past 0 (unless $1BAA is non-zero: then $1BAA is counted instead, the clock-stop item); at 000 it sets $1BB9 and jumps to $B5E9; drawn by $37A1 at sprite positions $6D-$6F; read by the stage-complete screen ($F269, $F289) for the time bonus.
Middle digit of the time in $CF86-$CF88.
Last digit of the time in $CF86-$CF88.

Which land: 0-4 Jellyland, Pipeland, Spottyland, Cherryland, Rockland; 5 the ending. $D76E sets it to $FF and $CBB0 increments it before each load, so a new game loads land 0; it picks the file name ($CC00), the loading text ($CC1A, $CC34, and $1096 for its colours) and the start-up path ($CE44). Also read by $3E86 and by $C9B5 (Jellyland's rule in $C955).
Continues left: 3 at a new game ($E54C); $3EAF decrements it, $10C1 increments it, $3DF9 and $3EAA read it.

A 0/1 flag kept while the land is happy ($1BEC): $3753 sets it when the count in $CF83-$CF85 falls below the land's $904A-$904C, $36BA clears it when the count climbs back to $904D-$904F. While it is set $F0E5 cycles the colour at $18E4. Cleared at the start of a land ($E569). Also read by $2B4C, $36A6, $373B, $38F3 and $3A9D.

The score digits as last drawn: $3578 redraws a digit of $CF78-$CF80 only where it differs from its copy here. Set to $FF by $E52D and by $3BA3 (at the start of a stage) to force a full redraw, refreshed from the score by $3513.
Drawn copy of the score's ten-millions digit $CF79.
Drawn copy of the score's millions digit $CF7A.
Drawn copy of the score's hundred-thousands digit $CF7B.
Drawn copy of the score's ten-thousands digit $CF7C.
Drawn copy of the score's thousands digit $CF7D.
Drawn copy of the score's hundreds digit $CF7E.
Drawn copy of the score's tens digit $CF7F.
Drawn copy of the score's units digit $CF80.
The count $CF83-$CF85 as last drawn ($36C3 copies, $3762 compares).
Drawn copy of $CF84, the middle digit of the dust/stars count.
Drawn copy of $CF85, the last digit of the dust/stars count.
The time $CF86-$CF88 as last drawn ($37D4 copies, $37A1 compares).
Drawn copy of the time's tens digit $CF87.
Drawn copy of the time's units digit $CF88.
Six little-endian pointers, $8A00, $8B00 ... $8F00: the pages of the land's tile tables. $25F7/$25FD copy pointer X into the LDA at $2603, which reads entry Y of each page.
High bytes of the pointers at $CF9B ($8A-$8F), read at $25FD into the high byte of the LDA at $2603.

Eight runs of colour numbers, each ended by $10: $CFA7 (5), $CFAD (8), $CFB6 (12), $CFC3 (7), $CFCB (10), $CFD6 (9), $CFE0 (7), $CFE8 (10). They are the object colour lists 0-8 (list 7 repeats $CFC3), reached through the pointer tables $B6BA/$B6C3 by $BF7F and $EB76 and stepped by $B645; the stage-complete raster handler also steps through $CFD6 ($F375).

Colour list 5 of the objects (the items' colours: $C9C4 picks it through $B6BA), and the colour run that the stage-complete handler steps through: $F375 reads entry $39 and wraps when it meets $10 (9 colours: $07 $0A $02 $03 $0E $06 $0D $05 $0B). The handler only compares the value it reads.
Thirteen bytes after the colour runs ($B4 00 00 00 FF BC BD FF FD B4 FC FD FB) with no reader found by absolute address; unknown.

The 1541 fast loader's 256 bytes of drive code, kept in the RAM under the VIC registers: the land loader swaps this page to $4000 ($3F54 entry 6) and writes it to the drive's $0700 in M-W commands ($CD3F), then starts it with M-E $07AB. With the I/O in, the address is sprite 0's X register instead, which $1A0C, $34A3, $4631, $B1E4, $BFBE, $C03E, $C09E, $C0F9 and $E1E6 write (most of them indexed stores that cover the other sprite registers too).

Start of 1.5 KB ($D100-$D6FF) kept here and run at $6000-$65FF: $3F54 entry 7 swaps these six pages with $6000-$65FF, from $3BC1 just before $3BC9 jumps into it at $638D (here $D48D), and $3BCC swaps them back when the scene ends (the scene's own last JSR $3F54, at $64F2 here $D5F2, has X = 0: swap 0, $D800-$DFFF with $7800-$7FFF). This first part ($6000-$635F when swapped in) is not decoded here; the sprite pointers $80, $82 and $83 that its code writes select images at $6000-$60FF, so it holds at least those, and it holds the routine $6300 (here $D400). The scene is played between the sad and the happy half of a land: $3BC6 loads the star quota just before it and $3BD1 restarts play with A = 1 after it; by the features it is presumably Theo's cave, not checked live. Not disassembled in place, since its addresses only make sense at $6000.
Code of the scene block as it runs at $6360-$638C (called from $64CD); see $D100. Kept as bytes because its addresses are those of $6000.

The scene's entry as it runs at $638D: fills the screens ($1A1C, colour 8, glyph $EE), places seven sprites from its tables at $659D-$65B8, patches the sprite bytes at $5812-$5825 ($E29F, $6573), sets the background colours $D021-$D023 from the land's $9196-$9198 and fills colour RAM $DADD-$DAEA (row 18, columns 13-26) with the land's $9199 ($63CD-$63D6), draws its picture rows into screen $4400 from $65B9-$65CA, zeroes colour RAM $D852-$D951 and $D8F2-$D9F1 ($640C-$6413), sets up the sound numbers $23, $22 and $21 through $3F0E (which $3F17, called at $D65E, requests one every second frame through $1352), installs its raster handler $64F8 through $1809 and then loops once a frame on stages kept in $1B3D (sprite movement, sound numbers $24-$26 and $27-$29 through $3F0E, $BE4A), until in stage 4 the fire button ends it: sprites off ($19BD), the SID silenced ($0D1B), $6573 with X = 0, swap 0 ($3F54 with X = 0: $D800-$DFFF with $7800-$7FFF) and JMP $3BCC, which swaps the six pages back. Its raster handlers are at $64F8 and $653F. Kept as bytes; see $D100.

The scene's tables as they sit at $658C-$65CA: four pairs of sprite bytes for $6573, the frame list $6594 (ends with 0), seven sprite positions ($659D), pointers ($65AB) and colours ($65B2), and the picture row read by $63DC-$63EC as $65B9,Y (Y = 0-$11), whose last byte is past this label, at $D6CA. See $D100.

The last 54 bytes of the swapped block ($65CA-$65FF when swapped in). The first, $D6CA ($AD), is the last byte of the scene's picture row: the loop at $63D8 (here $D4D8) reads $65B9,Y for Y = 0-$11. The other 53, $D6CB-$D6FF, look like note-and-length pairs ($BC $0A, $23 $7A ...); Jellyland's $9E74-$9E84 exchanges them, with the 110 bytes after them, with $7200-$72A2 ($01 = $24, X = $A3 down to 1). What they hold there is not established.

110 bytes ($D700-$D76D) after the swapped block, in the same note-and-length vocabulary ($BC $0A, $24 $03 ...). Outside the six pages that entry 7 swaps, so they never reach $6000 that way; Jellyland's $9E74-$9E84 exchanges $D6CB-$D76D with $7200-$72A2 ($01 = $24). Their meaning is not established.

Run by $CBAA with every ROM and the I/O banked out ($01 = $34): copies the default quota lines at $D77D ("MAGIC DUST QUOTA : 10", "STAR QUOTA : 113", 39 bytes) to $916F-$9195, where the loading screen prints them from (strings 19 and 20 of $B817), and sets the level index $CF89 to $FF so the next load is land 0. Each land's own file carries the following land's lines at those addresses.
"MAGIC DUST QUOTA : 10" and "STAR QUOTA : 113", ASCII, each $FF-terminated: Jellyland's quotas as the loading screen shows them, copied to $916F by $D76E.
91 bytes ($D7A4-$D7FE) of unknown use: 52 two-bit pixel-like values ($55/$5x/$Fx ...) to $D7D7, then $FF to the end; no reader found by address.

The byte before colour RAM (I/O meaning, $01 = $35): loops that run X from $FB down to 1 store through $D7FF,X so that X = 1 lands on $D800: filled with A by fill_screens ($1A1C); filled with 1 (white) by the protection screen's set-up at $4693. The RAM underneath belongs to the 2 KB block described at $D800.

Colour RAM, I/O meaning ($01 = $35 whenever the code runs): row 0, column 0. Zeroed by the level reveal at $1128-$1131 (X = 0-255 on each of the four pages $D800-$DBFF). Written by the level reveal's growing box ($119F, $11A9, $11E4: the land's $8900 colour for the character there, through ($4B)/($4D) set by $EFF7), which covers rows 0-23 from any of its five start rows. Filled with A by fill_screens ($1A26-$1A2F, X = $FB down to 1 from $D7FF, $D8F9, $D9F3 and $DAED). Written by the colour shift at $247C (X = 0-$25) from the cell 41 on (a row down, a column right). Written by recolour_column ($2550, from $2997, through ($3B)) with the land's $8900 colour for the character on screen: column 0 of rows 0-23. Written by the column drawer $27FF ($2840 through ($3E): the land's $8900 colour for each new character, 24 rows down from a column offset that follows the scroll). Read by the colour shift at $28E1 (X = $26 down to 0), which moves it down into row 1. Set to 1 (white) by the protection screen's clear at $4697-$46A0 (the same four bases and X range as fill_screens). These cell comments list the engine's own instructions; the intro and the ending write colour RAM with code of their own. Stage-card frame work, called from the card's raster handler $F1AC. On frames when $1B68 is set it scrolls a strip of 16 characters one pixel left, with wrap-round: glyphs $DE-$ED of the land's character set ($7EF0-$7F6F), all eight rows. Every frame it scrolls glyphs $FB-$FC ($7FD8-$7FE7) rows 0-4 two pixels, rows 5-7 of $FB-$FC with rows 0-2 of $FD-$FE by $BADC[$1B68] + 1 pixels, and rows 3-7 of $FD-$FE four pixels. Then sets all eight sprites from the land's tables: X from $910B, Y from $BADE (which $F1AC computes), pointers from $911B into $47F8, colours from $9123 (sad) or $912B (happy, $1BEC); all enabled, no X high bits.

Stage-card frame work, called from the handler $F1DA on frames when $1B68 is 0: scrolls three strips of four glyphs each ($7F78-$7F97, $7F98-$7FB7, $7FB8-$7FD7: glyphs $EF-$FA) two pixels left with wrap-round.

Called from the bottom raster handler ($212C).
